### Manako *(person · 8 ink · 42 pencil · 7 open · 47 GM-only)*

`manako` · threads: Manako and Cicada, Baldwin and organised crime, The Watcher

**How to play him.** Play him with no villain beats: no gloating, and no cruelty for its own sake. He never meant any of it. Every scene with him needs careful handling, so it leaks no secret and explains nothing early (D044).

**What people know**

- `manako.name` *(Ink)* The old man who owns the tea house is Manako, and he gives his name freely. — known some · told Episode One · The Errand · source D034, D045
- `manako.chemist` *(Ink)* Manako was a chemist for the Directorate, decades ago, and as a junior he was sent on the same errand the party gets. — known some · told Episode One · The Errand · source D018, D045
- `manako.came-back-empty-handed` *(Ink)* He came back from that errand empty-handed and was laughed at, and he has spent years going over what he should have done. — known some · told Episode One · The Errand · source D045
- `manako.the-vial-plan` *(Ink)* His plan: take the docket at its word and requisition a replacement vial, a real and expensive part, which needs a countersignature from a desk above the sender's and makes a form saying who asked, and why. — known some · told Episode One · The Errand · source D018
- `manako.disgraced` *(Ink)* He is the Directorate scientist who had a "breakdown" at a science conference, caused a huge fuss, and was expelled. — known some · told Episode One · The Errand · source D045
- `manako.district` *(Ink)* Manako's tea house is on The Slope, the hillside district of the city where he has a lot of influence. — known some · told Episode One · The Errand · source D046, D067
- `manako.ostracised` *(Pencil · hers)* Manako was ostracised for trying to warn people. — known some · told later · source D068, D070
- `manako.voice` *(Pencil · Claude)* Unhurried, precise, warm: an academic's diction worn soft by decades out of academia. Delighted by a good question, and visibly out of practice at being asked one. He talks freely about his past and never about the Watcher. He is openly bitter about the Directorate and fatherly to recruits (D045), which is part of why he makes an effective cult leader. He handles the object before he speaks: turns it over, holds it to the light, reads the back. He answers the question asked, then the better question they should have asked. He apologises for talking too much, and carries on talking. He speaks of the Directorate with perfect courtesy and no warmth whatsoever. — known some · told later · source D071, D045, D073, D081
- `manako.name-means-eye` *(Pencil · Claude)* Manako is an old word for the eye: a man called Eye, whom nobody would look at. The thing he found grew eyes. — known some · told later · source D073

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `manako.cicada` *(Ink · GM-only)* Manako founded Cicada. The Directorate has never linked the tea-house owner to the cult, and the party must make both discoveries themselves: that Cicada has an author, and who. — known few · told later · source D016, D017, D034
- `manako.messages-read` *(Ink · GM-only)* Trainee messages are read: by the Directorate as routine policy, and by the Watcher, which reads what is typed. A player who messages Manako is read too. — known few · told later · source D045
- `manako.underworld-dealings` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Manako has dealings with the underworld: he provides the crime lords with things, and they give him the ways to get noticed. — known few · told later · source D028, D068, D070
- `manako.was-warning` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Manako tried to upset the order of things to warn people about something invisible in their midst. While Manako was ostracised, powerful people looked into his warning and started to suspect he was right. — known few · told later · source D068, D070, D081
- `manako.the-sample-and-the-spill` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* About forty-four years ago Manako, a junior Directorate chemist, was given a shelved sample nobody senior wanted, catalogued as Inert 12. It was Sap. He cracked the capsule and spilled some on a tentacle of the Watcher that was nearby: the Sap fed it and made it visible, and Manako panicked. He knocked over a Bunsen burner and started a small fire in the lab. After the spill he lost his career for telling the truth: he was disgraced, with Shucks supervising. — known few · told later · when about 44 years ago · source D071, D039, D040, D073, D081
- `manako.the-fragment-that-stayed` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* A fragment of the Watcher stayed near Manako and helped him work out how to make more Sap. He became its first supplier, and he thinks it is a god. He doesn't know what he is to it. For a while he believed he was cursed: the thing seemed to follow him wherever he went. In fact it was waiting to see whether more food turned up, the way a dog follows a man who once fed it. — known nobody · told later · source D071, D073, D081
- `manako.saw-the-sky` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* About forty years ago Manako proved it to himself, privately: he learned to treat a lens and saw the whole sky full of it. — known nobody · told later · when about 40 years ago · source D071, D039, D040
- `manako.the-conference` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* About thirty-eight years ago Manako set off a canister of the chemical at a conference, to prove it: in a crowded hall, without warning anyone, having first checked that the Watcher was there. Eyes and tentacles writhed for as long as the dose held, and the room decided it was mass hallucination and concluded that a colleague had gone off the deep end. — known few · told later · when about 38 years ago · source D071, D040, D073, D081
- `manako.the-circle` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* After the conference a small, peaceful circle formed around Manako. — known few · told later · when about 38 years ago · source D071
- `manako.what-he-wants` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako wanted one thing, to be believed, and he was right. His need to prove the thing was real began as damage control after his disgrace: he wanted to defend the blunder that had ruined him, more than to understand it. Before Aoi died he wanted the city to see; after, he wanted the city to pay, and he stopped being particular about who helped. His tragedy is not that he's wicked. It is that he's right about the sky and wrong about what it is; that he's feeding the thing whose first hello got his wife killed; and that the party are the first people with any authority to believe him, and the ones who have to stop him. — known nobody · told later · source D071, D073, D028, D081
- `manako.arms-length-work` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako works for criminals at arm's length so he never has to see what he's part of. He has never met whoever is at the top of the crime lords he works for, and doesn't know who it is. At first the crime lords' problems reach him on paper and leave as solutions, and whatever they become happens somewhere he never goes. Each job sits a little closer to what it is for, and each time he finds a reason not to look. When he finally sees it, he accepts it without enjoying it. He is kind to strangers because he still thinks he's the man he used to be. — known nobody · told later · threads organised-crime · source D071, D068, D073, D031, D032, D081
- `manako.moods` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako's mood moves with the campaign, and it changes his children: a patient man's are aimless, a delighted man's are showy, a cornered man's are wasteful, a frightened man's are enormous. — known nobody · told later · source D071
- `manako.appearances` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The party meets Manako in person only a few times in the whole campaign: at the tea house in Chapter 1, perhaps for the lens lesson in Chapter 7, and at the accusation in Chapter 12. Between those, one of them may have his number. Manako crosses the party's path perhaps four times in all. He is met early as a kind stranger; what stays late is the party realising who he is. In Episode One, at the tea house, he solves a docket the Directorate couldn't, says one true thing about the Directorate, and opens a way to reach him. — known nobody · told later · source D071, D073, D016, D081
- `manako.his-number` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* If a player impresses Manako in Episode One, or is especially kind to him, the GM puts his number in that player's phone. That player can message him, or never do. — known few · told later · source D071, D045
- `manako.frail` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako is elderly and physically frail, no longer fit to fight. He runs the physical side of everything Cicada does from that frailty, and has spent decades biding his time, building, and choosing the moment. — known few · told later · source D073
- `manako.petty-crime-chemist` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Ingredients were expensive. After the disgrace Manako stole lab supplies, lost another job over it, and made ends meet as a chemist for petty criminals: small jobs, done by a man who was not a bad person and didn't think of himself as a criminal. The real slide came after Aoi. — known few · told later · source D073, D031
- `manako.the-failed-demonstration` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Before the conference, Manako tried to show his colleagues. The chemical worked perfectly, but the Watcher had moved on, so nothing happened, and he was finished as a serious person. He still has the speech he gave that room, and could give it again; its words aren't written yet. — known few · told later · source D073
- `manako.checks-first` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* After the room where nothing happened, Manako learned to check first: to track where the Watcher's attention was pooling before he staged anything. It is the technique in his discredited papers, which the party recovers in Chapter 4. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `manako.its-steering` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Watcher wants what it wants on its own account, but it had no personality to want it with. Drowning in a world it couldn't take in, it took the shape of the strongest coherent signal it could find, and for decades that has been one bitter man. Manako's grievance steers how it pursues its objective; the objective was never his. He is its steering, and its supply. Read backwards, its behaviour is a portrait of Manako. It grew eyes and ears above all else because he wanted to be seen and heard; it goes to loud gatherings because he was humiliated in front of a hall of colleagues; it shows you the Reel, so you know it learned from you, because a man who was disbelieved can't bear to be underestimated twice. What each of its children is doing answers to a fact about him, so the party assembles his portrait by fighting them, without knowing it. — known nobody · told later · threads the-watcher · source D073, D031, D081
- `manako.the-echo` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako believes he is a faithful worshipper interpreting divine intent. There is nothing to interpret: every instruction he has received was his own grievance handed back to him, wrapped round an appetite that was never his. The sentence that breaks him: he was never believed, he was echoed. The thing that confirmed him never had an opinion of him. It had an objective, and he was useful to it, as its shape and as its supply. He can't be argued out of his belief. He can only be shown, by watching the Watcher take a different shape for someone else, in front of him. He spent his life demonstrating, and a demonstration is what defeats him. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D081
- `manako.half-suspects` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako already half-suspects he was only ever echoed, and has spent forty years arranging his life so the question can't be asked: Cicada is partly a structure for not confirming it. He doesn't suspect the other half, that it has been feeding through him. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `manako.killing-or-capturing-him` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* The party meets Manako early and crosses his path now and then, but they can't kill or capture him early on. His main henchmen are the recurring fights. The party may kill Manako: that is their choice to make, and it is the wrong one. Without him the Watcher becomes a dangerous, unguidable problem. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D016, D078, D031, D081
- `manako.gifted-chemist` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Manako is an extremely gifted scientist and chemist, and was not a bad person at the start. His angry ambition, and his need for money, came after Aoi's death. — known few · told later · source D073, D031
- `manako.ways-to-be-noticed` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* In return the crime lords give Manako ways to be noticed: venues, crowds, printers, permits, a touring circuit, and people who know how to move crates through a harbour at night. Everything a man who wants to be seen needs, and can't get honestly. — known few · told later · source D073, D028
- `manako.list-worked-by-inner-circle` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako began his revenge list after Aoi died, and the inner circle works through it under cover of "tangential" missions. Shucks is on it as the institutional author of his ruin; Nobu is the personal one. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `manako.directorate-may-know-him` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* The Directorate may know Manako: he is the scientist it employed, and disgraced, decades ago. It may suspect that the Manako who runs the tea house is that same man, and that doesn't alarm it; it may even salve its conscience to see him still about and running a successful small business. It has no link between the kindly old man in the tea house and the cult. — known few · told later · source D073, D034
- `manako.desperation` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako's escalation is desperation, not ambition, and the Directorate winning causes it. The party finds a mark, traces a supplier, catches a courier; he is old and can't replace what he loses, so his time compresses, and he reaches for riskier sites, bigger doses and assets he would never have spent a year before. As he is cornered, he stops asking the Cadre how they got the precursors: a choice not to look. When the Young One kills someone in a heist, Manako finds out afterwards and does nothing, and that is the moment he becomes culpable. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D016, D081
- `manako.five-movements` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako's arc runs in movements, each turned by something the party does. The Patient Man: serene, kind, in no hurry; he wants to be believed, and it turns when somebody finally takes him seriously. The Delighted Man: energised, generous, dangerously flattered, helping them and correcting their mistakes; he wants to be understood, and it turns when they start winning and his assets fall. The Cornered Man: brittle, out of time; he wants to finish before he dies, and it turns when he learns he was a subcontractor, not a prophet. The Frightened Man: he has begun to suspect the echo; he wants it not to be true, and only being shown turns it. — known nobody · told later · threads manako-and-cicada · source D073, D016
- `manako.frightened` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Frightened Man is the dangerous one: he does large, loud, expensive things to keep the question of the echo unaskable. It isn't a plan; it's a man shouting. He can live with being a monster, because a monster chose something. He can't live with being an echo, because an echo never chose anything. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `manako.wrong-model` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako is a reliable narrator of everything except the one thing that matters. He talks freely, sincerely and accurately, and everything he says builds the wrong model, held more confidently the more time the party spends with him: closeness deepens the error. The truth lives elsewhere, in Hori, the museum fragment, the sceptics and the Watcher's own behaviour. He would never call it wreckage; he'd deny it, and mean it. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `manako.voice-by-movement` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* His later movements change his register and nothing else. Delighted: faster, more generous, more corrections. Cornered: shorter sentences, and he stops apologising for talking. Frightened: he talks over things. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `manako.what-not-to-do` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* What not to do. Don't make him mysterious at the first meeting: no significant pause, no watching them leave, no ominous parting line; he helps, and then he finishes his tea. Don't play him as insane or evil (D016); once he has accepted what he is becoming he does monstrous things, still never with relish. Don't have him lie. Don't let him recruit them on day one: he says one true thing and offers a way to reach him, and that is all. Don't have him explain the Watcher: he would explain it wrongly and sincerely, and an improvised cosmology risks putting the real answer in his mouth. Don't hand the table the conclusion: his name is free, but no one ever tells the party that Cicada has an author, or points at him (D017). Don't let his lines sound written: real speech hedges, trails off, repeats itself and reaches for the plain word, and a clever, symmetrical, self-aware turn of phrase is the failure to look for. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D016, D017, D044
- `manako.arc-is-the-spine` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako's arc is the spine of the Cicada half of the campaign, and his state shapes what manifests. Defeating him, alive, doesn't end the threat: the Watcher's objective is its own. What it buys is a Watcher that stays guidable. Once Manako understands what he is, he becomes the only living being with four decades of hands-on experience shaping the swarm, and so the only one who can un-shape it. What he can change is how it pursues its objective, never the objective itself: he can keep it steerable on the road to the mitflit home world, but can't talk it out of wanting to multiply. If it happens it is redemption as labour, done in front of everyone he hurt, not forgiveness. — known nobody · told later · threads manako-and-cicada · source D073, D031, D042, D081
- `manako.suspects-nobu` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Manako suspects Nobu of funding the column, but can't prove it. It is held in reserve as a reveal. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `manako.slide-and-movements` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The slide and the movements fit together. Before play, fifteen years of arm's-length work for the crime lords let him believe he is not so bad, which is why the kindness at the tea house is real: he still thinks he is the man he used to be. In the Patient and Delighted movements the self-image holds: being taken seriously, then understood, is the best evidence in fifteen years that he is still that man. In the Cornered movement the distance goes, and he takes on being a monster as a role, without relish. In the Frightened movement he meets the one thing he can't accept. In the Useful movement he is past the role. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D031

Told in the plan: Chapter 4 (`manako.the-papers`); Chapter 12 (`manako.the-only-rope`, `manako.revenge-list`, `manako.the-papers-are-his`, `manako.the-bill`, `manako.subcontractor`).

Still hers: `manako.who-suspected`, `manako.books-iv-and-v`, `manako.tea-house-name`, `manako.what-he-makes`, `manako.arrested-after-the-envoy`, `manako.why-not-hori`, `manako.learns-about-nobu`.

### The Mayor of Kurose *(person · 1 ink · 4 pencil · 1 open · 2 GM-only)*

`mayor` · threads: The mayor and the police

**Notes.** A new character for the plot, whom the party can meet (D068). Ingram's brief: the mayor "can act as both a blessing and a curse for the group, someone who is their own agent and who protects the city and their own position equally." Not yet decided: how the mayor holds office, where and when the party first meets them, and what they ask of the party. Nothing is placed in the plan.

**What people know**

- `mayor.fan-of-directorate` *(Pencil · hers)* The mayor of Kurose is a big fan of the Directorate, because of the commercial impact it has on the city. — known everyone · told later · source D068, D070
- `mayor.support-forces-cooperation` *(Pencil · hers)* The mayor backs the Directorate so strongly that the Directorate and the city's police are forced into uneasy cooperation whenever a raid or other activity is carried out against organised criminals or dangerous cultists. — known some · told later · source D068, D070
- `mayor.glad-to-say-so` *(Pencil · Claude)* The city has done well out of the Directorate, and the mayor is glad to say so. — known everyone · told later · source D071, D068

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `mayor.crime-initiative` *(Ink · GM-only)* The mayor brings the party in as a sort of magical armed-response team, as part of an initiative to use the Directorate's resources to fix the rampant organised crime in Kurose. The party won't know it is the mayor for a long time. — known few · told later · source D084
- `mayor.own-agent` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* The mayor is their own agent, and protects the city and their own position equally. — known few · told later · source D068, D070

Still hers: `mayor.name`.

### Mother *(person · 7 pencil · 2 open · 9 GM-only)*

`mother` · threads: The Watcher

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `mother.ships-mind` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Mother is the generation ship's mind. At First Impact she was left behind in the ship, weakened, when the ship's eyes were torn out of it. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D071, D032
- `mother.the-fragment` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* A mislabelled fragment in a glass case at Kurose's museum is a fragment of Mother. It is a piece of the generation ship that was never pulverised: small, coherent and sane. It sat mislabelled in a display case for two centuries, and it remembers what the navigation system was for, and what it answered to. Mother may still be alive in it, weakened and unable to control the Watcher directly, but a witness to everything and a source of information the players can reach. — known nobody · told later · when about 200 years ago · source D071, D041, D072, D032, D081
- `mother.proof` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* On the mitflit home world the fragment of Mother is the party's only proof, with the search ship itself, that they speak for the generation ship's descendants. — known nobody · told later · source D071, D041
- `mother.met-by-the-four` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* In the old campaign the four founders met Mother, a level-15 incorporeal construct, in the mitflit village beside the generation ship and on its cargo deck. She was the ship's reasoning core, with a chamber of her own on the bridge deck. — known few · told later · when 4721 AR · source D072, D031
- `mother.old-campaign` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* In the old campaign Mother was a level-15 incorporeal construct of great intelligence, met in the mitflit village inside the jungle ship and again on its cargo deck. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D032

Told in the plan: Chapter 6 (`mother.faint-voice`); Chapter 11 (`mother.speaks-clearly`).

### The natural history teacher *(person · 2 pencil)*

`school-natural-history-teacher`

**What people know**

- `school-natural-history-teacher.collector` *(Pencil · Claude)* The natural history teacher teaches what lives in, on and under the island: the drains, the tide-line, the flooded levels below the old works and the sea around them. A collector: her room is full of trays, jars and pinned things, almost all caught within a mile of where it sits. She is enormously, unguardedly enthusiastic about animals most people would rather not think about. She is the only teacher in the building who will happily tell a class she doesn't know what something is. Her register is the opposite of the history teacher's: she teaches what she has personally caught and is delighted by the gaps. A student who wants a true answer gets further with her, and the campaign shouldn't make that a secret. — known some · told later · source D075, D081
- `school-natural-history-teacher.the-specimen` *(Pencil · Claude)* She keeps in the cabinet a specimen she cannot classify, and says so cheerfully. It is a plant and nothing more: it is never explained in Episode One or Two, and isn't connected to Frame technology or First Impact. If a player connects it, that is theirs. — known some · told later · source D075

### Nobu *(person · 1 ink · 7 pencil · 2 open · 7 GM-only)*

`nobu` · threads: The Directorate, Manako and Cicada

**What people know**

- `nobu.quartermaster` *(Pencil · Claude)* Nobu runs Kit Issue and the budgets: harried, and generous in small, unexplained ways ("Right. Section Nine. I've got you."). He is who the party argues with about repairs. His generosity is impulsive, never deliberate: he does the generous thing too fast to examine it, doesn't make eye contact while he does it, waves off any thanks at once and changes the subject. Shucks watches a kid closely while being kind; Nobu looks away. He reads as a man compensating for something, not a man at peace with the institution. Shucks is warm because he has infinite time; Nobu is generous despite having none. — known some · told later · source D071, D075, D081
- `nobu.opinions-on-gear` *(Pencil · Claude)* Nobu has issued the kit list ten thousand times and has genuine favourites: asked what he would take himself, he tells you at speed, and he is right. A short, specific, well-aimed request gets results; a vague one loses to the queue behind you. — known some · told later · source D075

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `nobu.off-book` *(Ink · GM-only)* Some of what Nobu hands out isn't Directorate stock. He buys it for cash from the ships' chandlers on the old town's waterfront, because issue never arrives on time. — known few · told Episode One · Kit Issue · source D059
- `nobu.lab-assistant` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Forty-four years ago Nobu was Manako's lab assistant. He saw the tentacle too, and wouldn't back Manako up, because he thought the chemical had made them both see things. — known nobody · told later · when about 44 years ago · source D071, D039
- `nobu.the-debt` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nobu stood by and said nothing when it mattered, watched a man's life come apart, and kept his job. He has risen through procurement since: he runs Directorate procurement (materials, permits, budgets) and now controls the pool of technician-days that repairs and upgrades the Frames, so he is who the party argues with about repairs, and who the Caretaker has to beg for every accommodation. She thinks him unusually kind. He is paying a debt she knows nothing about. He believes he is making amends. A man with a guilty conscience and signing authority is exactly who the crime lords recruit. — known nobody · told later · source D075, D073, D039, D081
- `nobu.hides-well` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nobu isn't hiding badly; he is hiding well, with decades of practice. He is never nervous, evasive or cagey, and nothing in his manner gives his secret away. — known nobody · told later · source D075
- `nobu.rules-on-the-sit-in` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nobu controls the technician-day pool, and Bobbin is occupying a Frame, so Nobu must rule on the sit-in. The man secretly funding the enemy has to decide whether to authorise a forced extraction that would kill a pacifist. He will do the right thing for entirely the wrong reason, and nobody will ever know why. — known nobody · told later · source D078

Told in the plan: Chapter 9 (`nobu.the-funding`).

Still hers: `nobu.knows-whose`, `nobu.particulars`.

`noodle-stand-owner`

### Nozomi *(person · 7 pencil · 2 open · 7 GM-only)*

`nozomi` · threads: The Directorate

**What people know**

- `nozomi.name-on-the-board` *(Pencil · Claude)* Nozomi's name is struck through, in older chalk, on the Hangar Two board, under the six names. — known some · told Episode Two · The Names Are Still Up · source D071, D044
- `nozomi.locker` *(Pencil · Claude)* Nozomi's name is still on the roster and her locker is still assigned, though she declined the draft and is in questioning. — known some · told later · source D074, D002

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `nozomi.the-show-and-the-refusal` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nozomi was slated as the presumptive first pilot: the seat the party's own pilot ends up filling instead. Weeks before intake she went to what she thought was an ordinary private illusionist show. It was a Cicada recruitment drive: the performers revealed the Watcher filling the room, then demonstrated, undeniably and not as illusion, that it was real. She was shown something true and given an honest choice by people who didn't lie to her. She stayed to hear them out, and a high-level cultist told her, specifically and personally, that she was working for the wrong side: a targeted statement aimed at a presumptive Frame pilot. The next day she declined: she turned off her beeper and phone and avoided being drafted to fight. No violence, no scene, no confrontation on record: just absence. — known few · told later · source D075, D002, D081
- `nozomi.how-to-play-her` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nozomi is not a traitor, a villain or a coward. She thought it through under real pressure and made a considered decision; she did not panic and was not tricked. She is tired of repeating herself to the wrong kind of asking, not unwilling to talk. A conversation that doesn't ruffle her feathers gets somewhere; one that pushes or treats her like a suspect makes her go quiet, and may burn the chance for anyone else to try. A real, failable social challenge with a genuine cost. — known few · told later · source D075, D002, D081
- `nozomi.a-fragment-only` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* What the party can overhear of her search in the intake queue is a fragment, even on a critical success: it makes a sharp player wonder, and is never a resolvable lead. A later beat may not build directly off it without a real, separate scene making it actionable. Her absence is the reason the party exists, not a mystery to be solved in Chapter One. — known nobody · told later · source D075
- `nozomi.peril` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nozomi's jeopardy depends entirely on when and how she is found. She is saved by being reached before things split and force her to choose a side. — known few · told later · source D078

Told in the plan: Chapter 2 (`nozomi.the-interview`).

Still hers: `nozomi.what-she-says`, `nozomi.reappears`.

### The Section Officer *(person · 3 ink · 4 awaiting read · 12 pencil · 1 open · 12 GM-only)*

`section-officer` · threads: The Directorate, Section Nine, Rand's paper trail

**What people know**

- `section-officer.vetch` *(Awaiting read)* Section Officer Vetch runs Section Nine. He is never wrong in his own account. — known some · told Episode One · Assembly · source episode-c1e1--assembly
- `section-officer.the-docket` *(Ink)* On their first afternoon, Vetch sends Section Nine into the city with a stores docket for COMPOUND, LEVELLING, BUBBLE, ONE (1): the bubble in a spirit level. — known some · told Episode One · Kit Issue · source D018
- `section-officer.the-drains` *(Awaiting read)* At supper on the first day, Vetch reads Section Nine the night's worst job in front of the hall: storm drain clearance under the old town, from Dock C at twenty-one hundred. — known some · told Episode One · Canteen · source episode-c1e1--canteen
- `section-officer.voice` *(Pencil · Claude)* Vetch is clipped, procedural and faintly aggrieved. He uses the passive voice about anything that went wrong and the first person about anything that went right. He says "as discussed" about things that were not discussed, answers a question by reading the relevant clause aloud, and calls the party "Section Nine", never by their names, not even individually, treating that as neutral rather than cold. His sample line: "I was doing this when you were at school. I'm aware some of you still are." — known some · told later · source D071, D075, D081
- `section-officer.middling-and-never-wrong` *(Pencil · Claude)* Vetch is middling in rank and middle-aged, with immaculate paperwork: the only thing he is unambiguously good at, and he knows it. He has total authority over everything between reveille and lights out, and none over anything that matters; the second fact is why the first is exercised so thoroughly. Vetch is never wrong in his own account. When the party does something he didn't expect, he pauses exactly one beat and then recasts it as the intention all along. A player who spots the pattern can get him to claim a plan in front of somebody, and he is then committed to it. — known some · told later · source D075, D018, D082
- `section-officer.not-dangerous` *(Pencil · Claude)* Vetch cannot get the party hurt, sent away or charged. The worst he can do is make a fortnight tedious, and he will. His weapons are technically permitted duties and awful-but-real army tasks: never sabotage, never a crime, never cruelty. — known some · told later · source D075, D018
- `section-officer.ongoing-problem` *(Pencil · Claude)* Vetch stays an ongoing annoyance for the start of the adventure while being the party's primary point of contact with the Directorate for many early events. He turns up in person at the end of tasks to collect, assess and push the party toward what is next. There is no plan to defeat him yet. — known some · told later · source D075

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `section-officer.hazing` *(Ink · GM-only)* Vetch sends every new section on a fool's errand because it was done to him, and he believes it builds character. The same was done to Manako, decades ago. — known few · told later · source D018
- `section-officer.drains-for-the-vial` *(Awaiting read · GM-only)* Vetch gives Section Nine the drains because of the vial requisition, or, if they came back empty-handed, for the laugh. He never says so. — known few · told later · source episode-c1e1--canteen
- `section-officer.the-job` *(Awaiting read · GM-only)* At Dock C, Vetch gives them the job in one line: power to the drainage line, clear the compactor feed, report to him when it runs. He waits for them at the top. — known few · told Episode One · The Walk Down · source episode-c1e1--the-walk-down
- `section-officer.orders-them-not-to-act` *(Ink · GM-only)* When the exercise at the end of Episode Two turns into real combat, Vetch tells Section Nine not to act. They are put where the only sensible or heroic thing to do is act, and they still get in trouble with Vetch for acting. — known nobody · told Episode Two · Unidentified Contact · source D084
- `section-officer.unredeemed` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Vetch is tedious, self-important and small, mediocre and comfortable. He isn't cruel or dangerous, and he is not a hard man teaching hard lessons. He never wins on the merits, never harms them, and is never redeemed: no late scene where he was secretly proud of them all along. He is still there at the end of the campaign, doing the same to the next intake, unredeemed. — known nobody · told later · source D071, D075, D018, D081
- `section-officer.the-hazing` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Vetch knows he was foiled over the vial, and has it in for the party however gracefully they handled it, even if they try to save his face. His punishment is personal rather than procedural cover: he keeps ramping up the horrible duties because he doesn't like them. The hazing is a repeated exchange, not one clean win: every fresh assignment is also a chance to score a point back by malicious compliance, by doing the awful task so well it turns on him, or by using his own procedure against him. It is always full-party work, so that six strangers become a cohesive unit and nobody sits idle. — known few · told later · source D075, D018, D082
- `section-officer.promoted-out` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The party is eventually promoted out of Vetch's section by proving him wrong and outperforming his expectations: they do something he said couldn't be done in front of someone senior, and he claims it was his plan. He is not removed, corrected or improved. Shucks's quiet word is why the win sticks. — known nobody · told later · threads section-nine · source D075, D018
- `section-officer.out-of-his-depth` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Something real happens and Vetch is out of his depth in front of the party. He doesn't fail heroically; he has no idea and defers. It is quiet, and the party notices. — known nobody · told later · source D075
- `section-officer.the-transmission-chain` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* It was done to Manako forty years ago, in a Directorate lab; it was done to Vetch; he does it to the party. Three people, the same institutional shrug, and it broke one of them. The difference is not character: nobody handed Vetch a century-old sample and then blamed him for what happened. Nobody says it aloud; the party may notice Manako was hazed the same way, and nobody points at it. — known nobody · told later · source D075, D018
- `section-officer.has-done-every-job` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Vetch has done every job he hands out, properly, and knows what a bad one looks like. He tests a surface with a thumbnail rather than looking at it. He cannot let a wrong statement about procedure stand, and an appeal made correctly in writing gets further with him than one made out loud. — known few · told later · source D075

### Shinobu Kudo *(person · 2 ink · 7 pencil · 3 open · 9 GM-only)*

`shinobu` · threads: The Watcher

**What people know**

- `shinobu.the-phone-in` *(Ink)* On an evening radio phone-in, a father tries hard not to shout: his seventeen-year-old daughter is being held without charge, and nobody will tell him where. Neither of them is named on air. — known some · told Episode One · Canteen · source D044
- `shinobu.detained` *(Pencil · Claude)* The Directorate held Shinobu in military lockdown at once, and their reasoning wasn't stupid: independent scientists had confirmed Sap inert, but the Directorate knew the only place Sap is found is inside an alien ship, and knew what it reveals. They detained a teenage girl on the working assumption that she might become something. Months of nothing followed: no symptoms, no incident. She was released under mounting public pressure from her father Kudo, who is very good at his job and very loud about it. Surveillance continued after release, and confirmed, repeatedly, nothing. — known some · told later · source D075, D081

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `shinobu.who` *(Ink · GM-only)* The girl on the phone-in is Shinobu Kudo, and the caller is her father, Kudo. She comes back into the story much later. — known few · told later · source D003, D044
- `shinobu.most-watched` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Shinobu is the most witnessed person in the city, and nobody involved in that is being cruel. The Watcher finds its way into her glass cell deep underground to watch her. She is the most-watched person in the city. She was an ordinary bystander, handled by the Directorate, her father and the crowd that once nearly killed her in ways that are individually reasonable and collectively monstrous. She knows more than almost anyone alive about what it feels like to be completely seen, and can say something about it that nobody else can; she is entirely willing to talk. Her name means to endure, and also to hide. She belongs to the Observed thread, alongside the stray and the Mass Clock: the throughline about what it costs to be seen. — known nobody · told later · threads the-watcher · source D072, D031, D075, D081
- `shinobu.the-colony` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Splashed point-blank with Sap, Shinobu carries a colony of the Watcher's nanites, and she is its favourite subject. She survived the lorry because of what she carries: the colony reinforces and repairs her, and she is very slowly becoming something. Part of the Watcher lives in her, so she is held in its attention more or less continuously, not glimpsed occasionally. — known nobody · told later · threads the-watcher · source D071, D003, D075, D081
- `shinobu.the-splash` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Shinobu was splashed point-blank by Sap at one of Cicada's demonstrations. The physical result was mild skin irritation and nothing else. At that range the swarm had enough of it on her and in her to build a colony there, and the colony stayed: a dense population of the Watcher's own nanomachines, qualitatively different from the glimpse-and-fade exposure most witnesses get. — known few · told later · threads the-watcher · source D075, D031
- `shinobu.the-cell` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Shinobu is held in a deep underground cell with glass walls, cameras on every face, and remote operators watching in shifts, permanently. The Watcher finds its way in anyway, to look at its favourite subject: its visits are surveillance, since nothing in the city is more worth watching than a colony of its own growing inside a person. Two watchers on one cell: the institution's cameras and the Watcher's attention. There is no cruelty in it anywhere: the Directorate is being careful, the operators are doing their jobs, the Watcher is only looking. She is going nowhere and is entirely willing to talk: a point-blank eyewitness the party can simply visit. What she would say is not scripted. — known few · told later · threads the-watcher · source D075, D031, D081
- `shinobu.peril` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Shinobu is not scheduled to die. The jeopardy is that the colony is mishandled, by the Directorate or by well-meaning rescuers; she is saved by the party understanding what she actually is before acting. — known nobody · told later · source D075

### Shucks Mordant *(person · 6 ink · 4 awaiting read · 27 pencil · 4 open · 35 GM-only)*

- `shucks.skeleton-and-voice` *(Pencil · Claude)* Shucks is literally an animated skeleton in a white coat and stethoscope, not a figure of speech. Breathe."), asks a question and actually waits, gives practical instructions before kind ones and means both, and compares candidates to relatives he processed decades ago. - `shucks.rand-conspiracy` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Rand is a conspiracy theorist, investigating what is actually happening in the city entirely on its own initiative. - `baldwin.workshops` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Baldwin's gangs carry weapons made by enslaved mitflits in his workshops. The missing mitflits of the gathering are taken for those workshops. The heist crews are Baldwin's, and they carry his mitflit-made weapons: every crew the party catches carries evidence of where the weapons are made. The trail past the plant runs on towards the crews' weapons and the workshops that make them, as far as the campaign wants and no further. — known nobody · told later · threads organised-crime · source D071, D032, D073, D081
- `baldwin.croglang` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Croglang is Baldwin's front. For the four founders' players, it's the old name of Baldwin's castle. — known nobody · told later · source D071
- `baldwin.is-the-one-above` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The someone above the crime lords is Baldwin. He isn't named when the money leads there. — known nobody · told later · source D071, D068
- `baldwin.the-hunters` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* In the old campaign Baldwin led the hunters who captured mitflit savants for their minds, and ran the Baldwin family's magical-weapons manufactory at Baldwin Manor, once Croglang Castle, at Volkheed on Kortos. His note, carried by the mage Regina Key and signed "WCB", read: "Mitflits are there in force now, including many 'savants' ripe for the taking. I am gathering forces for a procurement operation." The last the old table saw of Baldwin was an army prepared on the Gauntlight map, hunters, infantry, archers and mobs, set against the mitflits in the keep. — known nobody · told later · when about 200 years ago · source D075, D031, D081
- `baldwin.the-grudge` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* At Baldwin Manor an Inicrium battery pulled the Shadow Plane into the town and a shadow siege followed, in which members of Baldwin's own family were killed by accident, not by the four. He blamed the four anyway: "These criminals broke into my ancestral home... That's my fucking horse's leather on that Gnoll." (Hyuck had paid a thief to steal a hunter's horse and had its hide made into armour.) — known nobody · told later · when about 200 years ago · source D075, D031
- `baldwin.insanely-rich` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Baldwin was insanely rich, and that may have given him access to ways to stay alive. — known nobody · told later · source D075, D032
- `baldwin.criminal-lord` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Baldwin is a criminal lord who arms criminal gangs with incredible weapons, and those weapons are still produced by essentially enslaved mitflits: the same trade as two hundred years ago, grown. The four founders would be his natural enemies if he revealed himself. — known nobody · told later · source D075, D032
- `baldwin.why-mitflits` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Mitflits have a horrible characteristic: they are both extremely helpful when given the right tasks and fascinated by the production of technology. It is what makes them so easy to use, and Baldwin knows it better than anyone alive. — known few · told later · source D075, D032
- `baldwin.the-organisation-in-kurose` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The crime lord Manako works for, at arm's length, is Baldwin's organisation: an arms trade can keep a gifted chemist solving problems on paper for years without his ever seeing a weapon. Baldwin is the crime lord Manako works for, neither fully knowing the other. Nobu's laundering, the Fixer's crime partners and the heist crews all run through his organisation. The mitflits arriving in Kurose to go home together are poor, badly housed and eager to be useful, which makes them the easiest prey his workshops have ever had. The weapons are built from ship technology that leaked out of the Kortos site. — known nobody · told later · threads organised-crime · source D073, D032, D075, D081
- `baldwin.known-on-sight` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The signs of Baldwin build long before he does, each deniable on its own: impossible weapons in gang hands, missing mitflits from the gathering, a front company called Croglang, and a crime lord nobody has ever seen. None of them names him. When he does reveal himself, the four founders will know him on sight, and so will their players. For Hyuck it is also about a horse. — known nobody · told later · threads organised-crime · source D073, D032, D075, D081
- `baldwin.hunter-band` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The hunters William Charles Baldwin led were Aubert "Golden", Kirkham, Thompkins, McGuire, Connor, Campbell, Hunniford and Shackley, with hired lackeys and a mage, Regina Key, in his pay. They were rough outdoors types who went from tavern to tavern in Otari making loud pronouncements about Gauntlight, and Baldwin himself struck the killing blow on a gnoll in the woods. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029

Told in the plan: Chapter 4 (`baldwin.impossible-weapons`); Chapter 12 (`baldwin.above-the-crime-lords`).

### The Young One *(person · 16 pencil · 1 open · 13 GM-only)*

`the-young-one` · threads: The four lieutenants

**What people know**

- `the-young-one.as-the-party-meets-him` *(Pencil · Claude)* The Young One is a Directorate Frame pilot a year or two ahead of the party, a little competitive ("You're Section Nine? Rough. We got harbour patrol."). His name isn't chosen yet. He first appears in the canteen as an unremarkable pilot-track student, who eats in the same room as the party and has an opinion about their assignment. He is an elf. At the canteen he wears the candidate tunic buttoned to the throat exactly as issued, neat hair, a level half-smile: nothing in him hints at what he is. The uniform worn perfectly is a man hiding behind conformity. — known some · told later · source D071, D019, D073, D075, D081
- `the-young-one.the-rescue` *(Pencil · Claude)* At the end of First Contact, if the party is failing, a combat Frame flown by the Young One arrives and saves them, cool and competent. The party likes him, which is what his unmasking will cost. — known some · told Episode Two · First Contact · source D085

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `the-young-one.why-he-stayed` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Young One stayed because he was useful where he was, because he told himself he could do more from inside, and because he was frightened. He has never worked out which is the real one. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `the-young-one.intelligence` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* What Cicada gets from the Young One is intelligence: Directorate movements, rosters, deployments, which sites are watched and when. He isn't muscle. He is why the heists work, and what he passes on may also reach the crime lords, which he doesn't know. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D019
- `the-young-one.doctrine-afterwards` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Young One is twenty and untrained for it when a heist goes wrong and he kills someone in panic, unintended. Then he has to become a person who meant to: the doctrine comes afterwards, constructed backwards to survive having done it, the talk about witness needing a real cost. Manako panicked in a lab and built a religion; the Section Officer was hazed and passes it down; this boy panics in a warehouse and builds a belief: nobody has done anything evil, they flinch, and spend a life justifying the flinch. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D019
- `the-young-one.wants-permission` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Young One wants permission: somebody to tell him it was all right. Manako won't and can't, and is visibly embarrassed by him. The party might, which is a dangerous thing to put in their hands. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D019
- `the-young-one.how-he-fights` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Young One is young, fast, athletic and reckless: pilot-trained, so competent but not a specialist. He closes and commits, and doesn't manage his action economy. He gets more dangerous as he is hurt, not out of conviction but because he has already done the worst thing he will ever do. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `the-young-one.alone` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Young One has no escape: he leaves when he is finished or is dragged off by people who can't stand him. His counter is that he is alone: no Aid, no flanking partner, no covering fire, because the Cadre won't support him. Focus him and he goes down. He is the one who can genuinely be beaten. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `the-young-one.has-a-frame` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Young One has a Frame, a card held in reserve: if the campaign wants it, the party fights a Claimant and a Directorate Frame on the same field, and the Frame is on the wrong side, piloted by somebody they've had lunch with. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D019
- `the-young-one.voice` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Masked, the Young One is over-formal: a role he has only seen in his head, slightly too big for him. Out of the mask he is completely ordinary, and the party should recognise the voice before they are told. He quotes Manako slightly wrong, always, the way a fan misquotes a favourite line; Manako has noticed and winces. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `the-young-one.competitive` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Young One is confident, a little competitive and not actually malicious. He eats in the party's canteen and has an opinion about their assignment. He is the campaign's thesis running in a third generation: Manako panicked in a lab, the Section Officer was hazed and passes it down, this boy panics in a warehouse and builds a belief on it. — known nobody · told later · source D075

Told in the plan: Chapter 4 (`the-young-one.masked-fighter`); Chapter 10 (`the-young-one.the-killing`); Chapter 12 (`the-young-one.turned-at-a-show`, `the-young-one.misquotes`, `the-young-one.unmasked`).

Still hers: `the-young-one.name`.

## §2 Groups

### The Brass Choir *(group · 3 pencil · 2 GM-only)*

`brass-choir`

**What people know**

- `brass-choir.who` *(Pencil · Claude)* The Brass Choir is the jazz-club gang of the Slope, based at a club called the Blue Pigeon, where a band never stops playing and the instruments hide weapons. — known some · told Retrofit (Episode c3e1) · Civil Assistance: The Blue Pigeon · source D085

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `brass-choir.the-tempo` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Brass Choir fights to the beat of its band, so each member acts on the beat; stopping the music costs the gang its timing. — known nobody · told Retrofit (Episode c3e1) · Civil Assistance: The Blue Pigeon · source D085
- `brass-choir.the-service` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Brass Choir rents its back rooms to Kiri for private shows, and the Booking Office pays the rent. — known few · told Retrofit (Episode c3e1) · Civil Assistance: The Blue Pigeon · source D085

### Cicada *(group · 7 ink · 2 awaiting read · 43 pencil · 7 open · 45 GM-only)*

`cicada` · threads: Manako and Cicada, The four lieutenants

**What people know**

- `cicada.violet-marks` *(Awaiting read)* Small deep-violet marks, always the same shade, appear at head height on walls where crowds stand and wait: queues, tram stops, waiting rooms. — known some · told Episode One · The Road In · source episode-c1e1--the-road-in
- `cicada.upstanding-citizens` *(Ink)* The cultists are good, competent, well-educated people. Once defeated, they turn out to be upstanding citizens: not mind-controlled, drugged or coerced, but smart and motivated people. — known some · told later · source D084, D085
- `cicada.assumed-the-opposite` *(Ink)* Everyone assumes the cultists are the opposite of good, competent and well educated. — known everyone · told later · source D085
- `cicada.what-the-public-knows` *(Pencil · hers)* Some of what Cicada has done is public knowledge, but it has stayed below most people's notice. The party learns about it piecemeal, as they look into it. — known some · told later · source D024, D048, D070
- `cicada.thin-file` *(Pencil · Claude)* To the Directorate Cicada is a thin file and mostly a nuisance. — known some · told later · source D071, D034
- `cicada.harbour-road-clash` *(Pencil · Claude)* Some weeks before intake, Cicada clashed with the police on the harbour road, and Sap was released there. — known some · told later · source D071, D043
- `cicada.stencil-on-the-sea-wall` *(Pencil · Claude)* A violet stencil sits under the growth on the sea wall. — known some · told Episode Two · Slack Water · source D071
- `cicada.demonstrations` *(Pencil · Claude)* A Cicada demonstration is a release of Sap in several crowded public places at once, and the public reads it as a chemical attack. But nobody dies at a demonstration: Sap does no harm, and the only injuries come from the crowd moving. That is the first clue a careful investigator can find: a terror campaign with no dead isn't a terror campaign. — known some · told later · source D073, D081
- `cicada.marks-painted-over` *(Pencil · Claude)* Some walls have been marked and painted over again and again for a decade or more. — known some · told later · source D073

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `cicada.quietly` *(Ink · GM-only)* Cicada has operated quietly for a long time. It isn't violent or threatening, so it has stayed below most people's notice. — known few · told later · source D048
- `cicada.marks-meaning` *(Awaiting read · GM-only)* The violet marks are Cicada's. Its people mark walls where crowds wait, as places to show a crowd something one day. — known few · told later · source episode-c1e1--the-road-in
- `cicada.works-with-the-criminals` *(Ink · GM-only)* The criminals are working with the cult. At first the gang fights won't seem to connect to the overall plot; as the party wins them, it gets the chance to investigate the scenes of the fights and starts uncovering hints that the criminals are working with the cult. — known few · told later · source D084
- `cicada.attacks-the-investigators` *(Ink · GM-only)* Manako's cultists respond to the party's attempts to investigate by attacking them. Cultists are the other major branch of the party's combat, beside the criminals. — known few · told later · source D084
- `cicada.raid-finds-the-cult` *(Ink · GM-only)* Sometimes the party raids something it thinks is a criminal operation, and it turns out to be a cultist operation. — known nobody · told later · source D084
- `cicada.debrief-gives-it-up` *(Ink · GM-only)* The group learns slowly what the cultists are really like, because anyone taken alive gives up a small amount of it in debrief. — known few · told later · source D085
- `cicada.trail-and-origins` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Followed far enough, the cultists lead directly to Manako. Cicada's origins are non-violent: Manako's original aims and process were peaceful. On the way, the party can uncover Cicada's non-violent origins: the Envoy incident with Hori and Aoi, and Manako's tragic history. — known few · told later · source D068, D070, D028, D081
- `cicada.became-a-movement` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* After Aoi died, Manako's circle became a movement that wants the city to look up and see what is in its sky. — known few · told later · source D071, D028, D034
- `cicada.faithful-never-fight-back` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Faithful's non-resistance is doctrine, not weakness. Standing still while arrested, helping a stranger up while being taken into custody, is the point: a martyr who doesn't fight makes a better argument than a fanatic who does, and they know it. Most of them have never held a weapon for Cicada and never will. The "dangerous cultists" the police and the Directorate raid together are, in the main, the Cadre: the Faithful never fight back. — known few · told later · source D071, D068, D073, D081
- `cicada.public-face-and-hidden-core` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Cicada is a public religious movement with a clandestine core, and a real antagonist faction. Its people call it Cicada, and it never lies. In public it doesn't hide and doesn't recruit by deception, and when asked it doesn't lie about what it wants: its whole purpose is to make people look. It shows a true thing and lets the viewer's own reason finish the job, which is why it catches lawyers, scientists and good citizens; the pitch asks for nothing objectionable: this is here, and it must be considered. Most of its members are guilty of nothing but having seen something real and believed their own eyes. Behind that it is a revolutionary, clandestine organisation with a mission, and assets it will use force to protect; what it keeps hidden is the column, the money and the criminal logistics. — known few · told later · source D073, D081
- `cicada.prisoners-talk` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* A live, questioned Cadre member is worth more to the party than a dead one: names, sites, the revenge list, the money trail. That is a reason for the party to fight carefully, never a reason for the Cadre to fight softly. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `cicada.the-name` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The name describes how Cicada works: cicada nymphs spend years underground, then come out everywhere at once and make an enormous amount of noise. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.witness-is-the-goal` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Cicada aren't terrorists: terror is never the goal, witness is. Some of what they do is dangerous, and now and then fatal in its consequences. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.marks-paint` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The violet marks are sprayed in marine primer, chandler's stock. Three suppliers in the city sell it, all on the harbour side. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.believe-me-now` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Cicada's whole theology is one question: "Believe me now?" Manako's conference was the first try, and every manifestation since is the same act at a larger scale. Under it runs a gentler motive Manako rarely says aloud: the thing is in agony, and quieting the city is the only relief there is. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.cadre-duties` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Cadre runs the column, deals with the criminal supply chain, guards sensitive sites, and does the countersurveillance and enforcement Cicada needs to survive underground for decades. It is trained, armed and disciplined, and willing to use lethal force when the mission requires it. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `cicada.cadre-vanguard` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Cadre don't think of themselves as villains. They see themselves as a vanguard protecting something sacred from an institution that buried the truth once already and would do it again. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.inner-circle` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Inside the Cadre, closest to Manako, is a small inner circle, fond enough of him to volunteer for tangential, unethical or dangerous work: it is where his revenge list gets carried out. The Cadre's loyalty is to the cause; the inner circle's is to him, a difference the party can come to use. Clean outer layer, poisoned core, and the outer layer doesn't know. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `cicada.manners-are-its-cover` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nobody in Kurose discusses the show they went to. The city's own manners are Cicada's security, and why the cult stayed buried for decades. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.the-cover-industry` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Behind the shows is a whole cover industry: venues, performers, a touring circuit, booking ledgers and ticket receipts. It can be investigated on foot, through theatre paperwork, without going near a Frame. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.thefts-filed-low` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The chemical stock stolen under cover of demonstrations is unusual but harmless, so the thefts are filed as low priority and lost in the general chaos. Nobody has ever laid the two columns of dates side by side. Laid together, the demonstrations and the unsolved warehouse thefts lead to the goods, the goods to the plant, and the plant to the column: police work on foot, with no Frame involved. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `cicada.friction-with-crime-lords` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Cicada and the crime lords both profit from the heist loop and both resent it. The friction between them can be noticed early, and used. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.the-files-drift` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Detained cultists make files, and the files reach the party. Read in order, they drift: ex-thugs and drifters, then the obviously susceptible, then a chemist, a lawyer, a school governor, and a classmate. The drift is slow enough that nobody sees the pattern until it is personal. — known few · told later · source D073
- `cicada.no-infiltration` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* There is no infiltration plot. Most cultists are guilty of nothing but having seen something and believed it, and the Directorate will order them arrested. — known nobody · told later · source D073
- `cicada.no-leader-in-the-file` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Directorate's thin file on Cicada names no leader and doesn't assume it has one, and nobody is assigned to it: private showings, a mark or two, the odd arrest for a public nuisance, released without charge. There is no sealed file and no redaction: the institution doesn't know, and has never asked. — known few · told later · source D073, D017, D034
- `cicada.the-original-cultist` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* "The Original Cultist" was a working label for Cicada's unidentified founder, not final. Since the Directorate's file doesn't assume a leader at all, any such label in play will be one the party invents, for a gap in a file. — known nobody · told later · source D073, D017, D034
- `cicada.right-and-wrong` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Cicada and the Watcher are both written as right about some things and wrong about others, with real motivations that, once fully explored, read as logical and consistent, even as another self-interested party rather than plain villains. Manako's warning about the Directorate is true. — known nobody · told later · source D077, D016
- `cicada.recurring-four` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The four lieutenants carry the contact frequency, since Manako appears in person perhaps four times: they arrive, announce themselves, wreck something, fight a little and leave. Each has one gimmick, one want, an escape the party watches happen, and a counter that is fixed before the first appearance, so each is a locked door with a keyhole and not an authorial veto. The party defeats them when the story is ready, and not before. The Soldier is the worthy opponent and the Fixer the aide with the real complaint; the Young One is the escalation, and works because the other three have a code and he has none. — known nobody · told later · threads the-lieutenants · source D073, D016, D019
- `cicada.lieutenants-witnesses` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* All four lieutenants came to Cicada the same way: somebody showed them something true and they couldn't un-see it. None is a fanatic in the ordinary sense; they are witnesses, not believers. — known nobody · told later · threads the-lieutenants · source D073, D019
- `cicada.misreads-gen-2` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Cicada's theology reads the Watcher's attention as meaningful, so when the Watcher fixes on the new Gen 2 Frames it concludes the fixation is significant and then dangerous. It watches the thing it reveres reach for its makers' technology, reads divine alarm, and decides the new machines are blasphemous, dangerous or a rival power's doing, never landing near the truth. It is exactly as rational as its founder's worldview allows. — known nobody · told later · source D074, D020
- `cicada.farming-it` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Cicada is not revealing the Watcher, it is farming it. Every demonstration is a meal, and the citywide simultaneous emergence is a mass feeding event. Manako believes he is waking the city to a god; he has spent decades making one. — known nobody · told later · source D078
- `cicada.lieutenants-learn` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Each recurring Cadre lieutenant gets a stat block fitted to the level of the encounter, and they learn new tricks as the group fights them, so they stay a challenge and keep surprising the group. Each one's signature ability, escape, counter and voice never change; level and stats do, with exactly one new named ability per appearance. — known nobody · told later · source D078, D018
- `cicada.cultists-never-call-it` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* A Faithful in debrief says plainly that Cicada does not summon anything: it shows people something true and lets them decide. — known few · told Retrofit (Episode c3e1) · The Police Interview · source D085
- `cicada.children-form-after-they-leave` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* At every demonstration site the creatures form hours after the cultists have gone, never while they are there. — known few · told The Square (Episode c4e2) · The Square · source D085
