### The Directorate *(group · 26 ink · 13 awaiting read · 29 pencil · 6 open · 23 GM-only)*

`directorate` · threads: The Directorate

**Notes.** Ingram's own phrase for the armed-response team is "Magical SWAT Team" (D068). It stays in this note and out of anything the table hears. Missions against criminals and missions against cultists are the campaign's two main branches of personnel-level combat. The mayor's support for the Directorate is why such missions are joint with the police (`mayor.support-forces-cooperation`).

**What people know**

- `directorate.founded-after` *(Ink)* About five years after the rift, four of the people who had stood in front of it founded the Directorate, so that the response next time would be faster and more decisive. — known everyone · told from the start · when about 5 years after rift.opened · source S001, D024, D025
- `directorate.came-to-kurose` *(Ink)* About a hundred and fifty years ago, the Directorate crossed the world and settled in Kurose. — known everyone · told from the start · when about 150 years ago · source S001, D024, D025
- `directorate.why-kurose-unexplained` *(Ink)* The Directorate has never said publicly why it believes there will be another rift, or why it crossed the world to wait for it in a fishing village. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `directorate.public-view` *(Ink)* Kurose sees the Directorate as both a grand mission against a disaster nobody expects to see and a heavy-work corps everybody relies on, and people joke about the gap. — known everyone · told from the start · source D025
- `directorate.newcomers` *(Ink)* Hundreds of people from across Golarion moved to Kurose to be part of the Directorate. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `directorate.newcomers-built` *(Awaiting read)* The newcomers were engineers, clerks, scholars and pilots, and then the people who fed, housed and sold to them. They built streets and temples of their own. — known everyone · told from the start · source episode-c1e1--from-up-here
- `directorate.brought-wealth` *(Ink)* Not everyone trusts the Directorate, but few can argue against the vast wealth and technology it has brought to the area in so little time. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `directorate.answers-to-itself` *(Ink)* The Directorate recruits separately from Minkai's army and navy, and operates outside Minkai's national lines. — known everyone · told from the start · source D025, D026
- `directorate.warmongers` *(Ink)* The Directorate is a foreign army in the harbour: intruders, outsiders, even warmongers. — known everyone · told from the start · source D025 · held by many in Kurose, true: no, truth `directorate.founded-after`
- `directorate.protectors` *(Ink)* The Directorate is Kurose's protector. — known everyone · told from the start · source D025 · held by some in Kurose, true: yes
- `directorate.base` *(Awaiting read)* The Directorate's base is its own man-made island in the harbour, built up around a rock and reached by a long causeway with a railway line beside it. A flat grey fortress with no windows stands at its southern end, among hangars, workshops, offices and barracks, and a high fence runs round the whole island. — known everyone · told from the start · source episode-c1e1--from-up-here
- `directorate.gate` *(Awaiting read)* At the land end of the causeway is the gate: a red-and-white barrier across the road, a guard booth not much bigger than a telephone box, and a guard with a ledger. — known everyone · told from the start · source episode-c1e1--from-up-here
- `directorate.sends-for-trainees` *(Ink)* Every year the Directorate sends for new trainees. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `directorate.trainee-expectations` *(Ink)* Most people expect a spell as a trainee to be a faff and a bother: a duty which, once discharged, is done. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `directorate.how-trainees-come` *(Ink)* Some trainees volunteer, some are encouraged into it, and some are pushed into it. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `directorate.who-joins` *(Ink)* People apply to the Directorate, or are streamed on to it from school. — known everyone · told from the start · source D026
- `directorate.brought-forward-stamp` *(Ink)* Every candidate's acceptance letter this year has its printed reporting date ruled through, "Monday next" written beside it in pen, and a red BROUGHT FORWARD stamp. Nothing on intake day explains it. — known some · told Episode One · The Road In · source D038
- `directorate.form-12b` *(Ink)* Form 12-B, the intake screening form, asks for mother's maiden name twice: in box 4, and again in box 19, in capitals. — known some · told Episode One · Intake Medicals · source D038
- `directorate.section-nine` *(Awaiting read)* The six are Section Nine. Each of them was told, alone, that their screen came back irregular. — known some · told Episode One · Intake Medicals · source episode-c1e1--intake-medicals
- `directorate.school-and-service` *(Ink)* The Directorate is a school and a service at once: candidates sit lessons, and they also drill, carry orders and stand watches. — known everyone · told Episode One · Assembly · source D053
- `directorate.free-time` *(Ink)* A candidate's free time is theirs to choose: the gymnasium, the range, the library, or a lesson they pick themselves. — known everyone · told Episode One · Assembly · source D053
- `directorate.curfew-minor` *(Ink)* Breaking curfew is a very minor offence: it is written down, and the candidate is told off. — known everyone · told Episode One · Assembly · source D053
- `directorate.orders-serious` *(Ink)* Refusing a direct order is the most serious thing a candidate can do. It means a hearing in front of someone senior, to explain themselves. — known everyone · told Episode One · Assembly · source D053
- `directorate.alarm-never-real` *(Awaiting read)* In a hundred and fifty years, the Directorate's alarm has never once been real. — known everyone · told Episode One · Assembly · source episode-c1e1--assembly
- `directorate.intake-size` *(Awaiting read)* This year's intake is about forty candidates. The whole base turns out in the drill hall to welcome it. — known everyone · told Episode One · Assembly · source episode-c1e1--assembly
- `directorate.no-track` *(Awaiting read)* Every candidate's section card names a track as well as a section. The six Section Nine cards leave the track blank, and so does the clerk's list. — known some · told Episode One · Intake Medicals · source episode-c1e1--intake-medicals
- `directorate.on-report` *(Awaiting read)* A refused order goes on the candidate's file, and they are on report. If they are later proven right, that goes on the file too, in the Deputy Director's hand. — known some · told Episode One · The Errand · source episode-c1e1--the-errand
- `directorate.vials-to-medical` *(Awaiting read)* A requisition for a vial goes up to Medical for its countersignature: vials are Medical's. — known some · told Episode One · The Train Back · source episode-c1e1--the-tram-back
- `directorate.paper-name` *(Awaiting read)* On its own paperwork the Directorate is called Tokubetsu Taisaku Honbu, Special Countermeasures Headquarters. — known some · told Episode One · The Road In · source episode-c1e1--the-road-in
- `directorate.combined-campus` *(Awaiting read)* The combined campus named in the acceptance letter is the Directorate's island base. — known some · told Episode One · The Road In · source episode-c1e1--the-road-in
- `directorate.island-ways-in` *(Ink)* There are two ways onto the Directorate's island: by train, which becomes a tram at the causeway, or by two one-way car bridges that run under a huge bunker. — known everyone · told later · source D065
- `directorate.island-air-and-sea` *(Ink)* There is an airport on the island, and small boats dock at several places along it. — known everyone · told later · source D065
- `directorate.island-security` *(Proposal)* Security on the island is extremely patchy at the start of the adventure, because the Directorate cannot afford to upset the people of Minkai or Kurose, so it allows an uneasy balance of formal borders and informal oversight. — known some · told later · source D065
- `directorate.under-arms` *(Pencil · hers)* The Directorate has a large number of people under arms and training. — known everyone · told later · source D068, D070
- `directorate.clearance` *(Pencil · Claude)* Rank in the Directorate is Clearance, from 0 to 5, and each rank lets its holders do more: 0, Recruits, do as they're told; 1, Cadets, choose their duty and sign for small things themselves; 2, Duty Section, send themselves to a contact and interview detainees; 3, Officers, direct other units and call on a city asset; 4, Command, overrule a decision once a chapter and open sealed records; 5, Prodigies, the city does what they say. It is being believed, made countable. — known everyone · told later · source D071
- `directorate.response-roster` *(Pencil · Claude)* The response roster is the list of units the plotting floor calls out when something appears in the city. The party is put on it at the end of Chapter 1. — known everyone · told Episode Two · The Hammer · source D071
- `directorate.contact` *(Pencil · Claude)* "Contact" is the plotting floor's word for something appearing in the city, read out over the radio as a numbered track ("track forty-one"), and for the event itself. — known everyone · told later · source D071
- `directorate.claimants` *(Pencil · Claude)* The Directorate calls the things that appear Claimants, announced by code ("Claimant Three, contact confirmed") and never named. The first ones are called Proto-Claimants. — known some · told Episode Two · First Contact · source D071
- `directorate.vault-inventory-refused` *(Pencil · Claude)* The Transparency Advocate has asked three times for the inventory of what the Directorate keeps in deep storage, and been told it's held above their clearance. — known some · told later · source D071, D044
- `directorate.the-official-line` *(Pencil · Claude)* Cultists are summoning the things that attack the city. — known everyone · told The Roster Calls (Episode c2e1) · The Morning After · source D071, D035, D085 · held by the Directorate, and at first the party, true: no, truth `watcher.where-children-form`
- `directorate.two-ends` *(Pencil · hers)* The school and the base are one island with two ends, not one blended site. The north-west end (the causeway, the Roadgate, the Frame hangar, the workshops, the vehicle control point and the candidate camp) is pure military and checkpoints. The school is further south-east on the same island, and a candidate walks from one to the other. — known everyone · told later · source D077, D013
- `directorate.rite-of-passage` *(Pencil · Claude)* A century and a half of Frames, a charter, a chain of command, an anthem and a maintenance budget, and no war: the Directorate is a rite of passage, mildly boring, faintly prestigious, and entirely untested. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate.the-dig-is-public` *(Pencil · Claude)* The dig under Kurose is not secret: it is a public-works programme with a budget line. That is why the biggest fault in the institution is the one nobody looks at. — known everyone · told later · source D074
- `directorate.leaves-it-lying` *(Pencil · Claude)* The police court's hearing of Aoi's name never reached the Directorate, because the police and the Directorate distrust each other. Its line on the Envoy incident is only that a cultist was killed in a confrontation in which someone magically summoned a monster. — known some · told later · source D074, D035
- `directorate.consent-in-the-forms` *(Pencil · Claude)* The consent for the Directorate to read trainees' messages is in the intake paperwork: the same forms, handed over on day one, that ask for mother's maiden name twice and get laughed at. — known some · told later · source D074
- `directorate.pilots-roster` *(Pencil · Claude)* A wide roster of NPC pilots exists when the campaign starts, beside the party's six. Over the campaign they drop out one by one, some through the GM's story beats and some through consequences the players create, until the six are the only pilots left. It should land as attrition, paced against real beats, not a body count. — known everyone · told later · source D074
- `directorate.first-look-mix` *(Pencil · hers)* On first arrival the campus reads as a genuine, deliberate mix of military and school, and neither dominates. Both registers carry equal weight from the first look: the tonal dissonance is the point of the very first image, not something that reveals itself gradually. — known everyone · told later · source D078, D012

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `directorate.digs` *(Ink · GM-only)* The Directorate is Golarion's foremost gatherer of alien technology. It digs for it and locks it in deep storage vaults, so that it can't cause another disaster. — known few · told Episode One · The Errand · source D040, D044, D056
- `directorate.why-brought-forward` *(Ink · GM-only)* This year's intake was brought forward two weeks because Nozomi, the pilot expected to fly first, refused the draft after a magic show. — known few · told later · source D002, D011, D020, D038
- `directorate.forms-typed-ahead` *(Ink · GM-only)* Every candidate's Form 12-B is typed with their name before they arrive, on the same admissions typewriter as their acceptance letter. Its lower-case e strikes low and faint. — known few · told Episode One · Intake Medicals · source D059
- `directorate.missing-pilot-search` *(Ink · GM-only)* On intake morning, staff are quietly hunting for a pilot who hasn't turned up. A careful listener can catch the name Nozomi. — known few · told Episode One · Intake Medicals · source D011
- `directorate.the-marker` *(Ink · GM-only)* Some people carry a heritable marker in their blood. Only people who carry it can pilot the newer, second-generation Frames. All six of the party carry it. — known few · told later · source D020, D021, D034
- `directorate.carriers-streamed` *(Awaiting read · GM-only)* Candidates whose screen shows the marker are streamed into one section together, as routine. Six in a single intake has never happened before. — known few · told later · source episode-c1e1--intake-medicals
- `directorate.magical-swat` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* The Directorate brings the party in, as a sort of magical armed-response team, for certain missions against criminals and cultists. — known few · told later · source D068, D070
- `directorate.born-at-kortos` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Directorate was born from a coalition of the organisations around Kortos, banded together to guard the opened ship, with the four at its heart. It had two jobs: keep the promise, and make sure the response would be faster next time. It was also founded to guard the broken ship and keep its technology from destabilising the world. Early work with the ship's technology frightened the four badly. — known few · told later · when about 195 years ago · source D071, D040, D072, D032, D081
- `directorate.first-gen-1` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* When the Directorate came to Kurose it dug up the search ship's hull and built the first Gen 1 Frames: Golarion technology only, informed by what the Kortos site showed it, mechanical clankers with no living core. It dug to recover the ship's technology and lock it in deep storage vaults. — known few · told later · when about 150 years ago · source D072, D032
- `directorate.not-a-conspiracy` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Directorate is not a conspiracy. It is an institution that has never been tested, can't admit it, and is slowly harming the city it was built to protect, mostly by doing its job exactly as written. Nobody at the top coordinates its faults: they are separate departments being ordinary. The people of the Directorate are, with real exceptions, decent, tired, fond of the children and bad at their jobs in ways they can't perceive: Shucks, Nobu, Taka, the repair chiefs and the bridge staff are warm, funny and on the children's side. The faults of the institution are none of their doing and mostly beyond their power. — known nobody · told later · source D074, D081
- `directorate.kortos-coalition` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* The Directorate was born on Kortos about 195 years ago, when the organisations around the opened ship banded together to keep the site secure, prevent another rupture and stop the uncovered technology disrupting the world. The move to Kurose for the prophecy came later, and there it found the search ship. — known few · told later · when about 195 years ago · source D074, D032
- `directorate.unknowingly-calls-it` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The digging the Directorate does to keep the world safe is exactly what calls the Watcher. The institution can't see this, because it doesn't know the Watcher exists. — known nobody · told later · source D074, D040
- `directorate.secretive-not-evil` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Directorate is very secretive, not evil. What it hides, it hides in deep storage: the players may rightly start to wonder what it is hiding, and be right that it hides things. The vaults themselves can be mentioned openly, and the redacted-document chain used to point at them. What must not surface for a long time is anything about the demon that lives in one of the four. — known nobody · told later · source D074, D041, D033, D081
- `directorate.knows-gen-2-alive` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Directorate knows the Gen 2 prototypes are alive, and doesn't say so. — known few · told later · source D074, D032
- `directorate.paperwork-disappears-people` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Directorate makes inconvenient people administratively disappear without anyone deciding to. Aoi was filed as "one deceased, unidentified" because nobody thought her worth the paperwork; Shinobu Kudo was detained without charge; Nozomi, who declined the draft, is held in questioning while her name stays on the roster. Each is a department doing an ordinary thing. — known nobody · told later · source D074
- `directorate.acts-on-intercepts` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Later in the campaign the Directorate acts on what it has read: it moves on Manako or a cult site at a moment the party didn't choose, with information the party itself generated, and wrecks a plan they had. It is no individual's betrayal, only a clerk doing a filing job under a policy written decades ago by people who are dead, which is exactly what makes it one. — known nobody · told later · threads the-directorate · source D074

Told in the plan: Chapter 8 (`directorate.reads-the-messages`, `directorate.two-readers`); Chapter 13 (`directorate.deepest-vault`, `directorate.falls-to-the-six`, `directorate.vault-goal`).

Still hers: `directorate.school-name`, `directorate.seaward-platform`, `directorate.the-three-poles`, `directorate.who-decided-the-silence`, `directorate.who-wrote-the-policy`, `directorate.leak-a-fault`.

### The Directorate's posts *(group · 22 pencil · 1 GM-only)*

`directorate-posts`

**What people know**

- `directorate-posts.canteen-manager` *(Pencil · Claude)* Manager, The Works Canteen: Feeds the entire works strip in three sittings and knows, from who sits with whom, roughly everything about how the work is really going. Treats rank as a suggestion and pilots as young people who need feeding. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.chief-draughtsman` *(Pencil · Claude)* Chief Draughtsman, The Drawing Office: Runs the hundred metres of drawing boards where every part the works makes exists on paper before it exists in steel. Holds, more completely than anyone, the answer to how a Frame is actually put together. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.deep-storage-custodian` *(Pencil · Claude)* Custodian, Deep Storage: Runs the day-to-day of Deep Storage: decides what still counts as 'currently being used', signs off on requisitions, and is the one person who actually knows which underground floors are real storage and which are a number on a door that was never built out behind it. Answers, eventually, to whoever has the authority to decide what Deep Storage is allowed to hold, in practice the Commander's pole. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.generating-hall-engineer` *(Pencil · Claude)* Duty Engineer, The Generating Hall: Keeps the works in power, four sets, three running, one always stripped down. The person who decides which shop loses its supply first when the load will not stretch. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.goods-inwards-officer` *(Pencil · Claude)* Goods Inwards Officer, The Bonded Store: Signs for everything that comes onto the island under seal, and decides what goes to the Quarantine Shed when the manifest and the contents disagree. Wholly uninterested in who is asking. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.hospital-chief-of-staff` *(Pencil · Claude)* Chief of Staff, The General Hospital: Runs The General Hospital day to day, wards, staff, and who is actually allowed to see whom. The hospital nominally answers to Shucks Mordant as the Directorate's Chief Medical Officer, but he is never there in person; this is the person a party actually deals with. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.landing-end-duty-nco` *(Pencil · Claude)* Duty NCO, The Landing End: Whoever is standing duty NCO for the Landing End on a given watch, covers the maintenance log, the drain-cover checks after a high tide, and whatever else turns up on a quiet night shift that technically isn't in anyone's job description. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.plot-room-supervisor` *(Pencil · Claude)* Supervisor, The Plot Room: Runs the plotting floor: the table, the markers, the headsets and the people wearing them. Responsible for how out of date the city's picture of itself is at any given moment, and acutely aware of it. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.range-safety-officer` *(Pencil · Claude)* Range Safety Officer, The Proving Ground: Runs live-fire and manoeuvre qualification at The Proving Ground, the Frame- and vehicle-scale range east of the Gatehouse, not to be confused with The Butts (personnel small arms). Calls the line hot or safe from Range Control, and nothing fires without that call. The one person on the base whose 'no' on a Frame or a pilot is not really arguable in the moment, whatever the reason turns out to be. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.registry-clerk` *(Pencil · Claude)* Registry Clerk, The Registry: Works the records floor and the print room where every Directorate document is typed once per clearance level. Has read every version of everything and holds no clearance rung worth the name, an institutional absurdity nobody above them has ever noticed. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.switchboard-supervisor` *(Pencil · Claude)* Switchboard Supervisor, The Telephone Exchange: Runs the island's switchboard. Every call between any two parts of the Directorate is physically connected by one of their operators, which makes this small team the best-informed people on the island almost by accident. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.time-office-clerk` *(Pencil · Claude)* Clerk, The Time Office: Keeps the clocking-in cards for the whole strip. Holds, without anyone thinking of it as records, a minute-by-minute account of where several thousand people were on any given day. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.the-rock-research-director` *(Pencil · Claude)* Research Director, The Rock: Runs the laboratory side of The Rock, what is actually being studied, and why it needs a prison next to it rather than an ordinary research floor. What that research is remains an open question by design; this NPC is the person who knows the answer, not a vehicle for deciding it here. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.the-rock-warden` *(Pencil · Claude)* Warden, The Rock: Runs the prison side of The Rock, who is held in which of the nine cells, on whose authority, and under what conditions. Deliberately not one of the Directorate's three visible poles (Commander/Caretaker/Transparency Advocate): The Rock is classified Omega-Zero specifically because most Directorate staff don't know it exists, and giving it a publicly-known face would undercut that. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.vermilion-block-custodian` *(Pencil · Claude)* Reagent Stores Custodian, The Vermilion Block: Signs for every delivery into the six fenced silos north-west of the Block and every draw back out of them, the one paper trail that actually exists for what has come in from across Golarion in bulk. Not a spellcaster, by design: a custodian who could use what they store would be a security problem the Directorate would rather not create. Knows exactly how much is in each silo and exactly nothing about what any of it is eventually used for, which is precisely the arrangement their superiors want. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.vermilion-block-director` *(Pencil · Claude)* Officer in Charge, The Vermilion Block: Runs the Directorate's own magic-using department out of the black-and-red building on Island Centre marked with a red diamond hazard placard. Extremely high proficiency as a spellcaster themself, and the one person on staff whose sign-off actually means something when a reagent shipment, a test, or a request for magical support from another department needs approving. Most staff know the Block exists; almost none of them know this person's day-to-day work, only that requests go through them and answers come back slowly, if at all. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.works-manager` *(Pencil · Claude)* Works Manager, the south-west works: Runs the whole south-western works strip, the Erecting Shop, the Armour Shop and everything feeding them. Decides, in practice, what actually gets built this month and in which bay, which makes this the person whose goodwill determines whether a Frame is ready when it is needed. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.school-registrar` *(Pencil · Claude)* Registrar, Main School Complex: Runs placement testing and academic streaming for every candidate who passes through the Main School Complex, scores the tests, keeps the real archive on the second floor, and decides which section a student lands in. Sees the raw data behind every candidate's placement, which is more than almost anyone else on the island sees in one place, and has never been told why the Directorate wants it kept. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.school-civil-defence-instructor` *(Pencil · Claude)* Civil defence instructor, Main School Complex: Teaches shelter procedure, muster points and the four alert states, and has done for eleven years. A serving NCO rather than a teacher, which shows: she drills rather than explains, makes people repeat things back, and is entirely unhurried about doing it again. Nothing she teaches has ever been used, not once in a hundred and fifty years, and she will say so herself without it denting her conviction in the slightest. What she actually wants is not in the lesson. She has applied four times to have the alert-state drill reinstated as a real base-wide exercise rather than a classroom subject, and been refused four times, on cost. Her class is the only place the material still gets said out loud by anybody, and she knows it. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.intake-medicals-clerk` *(Pencil · Claude)* Records clerk, Intake Medicals: Runs Records at the Intake Medicals counter on the combined campus: flat, patient, entirely without irony, and has already explained today's form to more candidates than she's counting. Wants exactly one thing from each of them, the form filled in correctly, and has no other ambitions today. Hands out Form 12-B, whose box four and box nineteen both ask for a mother's maiden name, one copy for Records and one for Welfare, because the two departments haven't spoken since the flood; she isn't embarrassed by this, and explains it the same way every time. Answers the question she was asked and then stops talking. Short and solidly built behind the counter, sleeves rolled to the elbow; nothing about her reads as anything but a career civil servant who has been doing this exact job for a long time. She is a dwarf. — known some · told later · source D075
- `directorate-posts.repair-chiefs` *(Pencil · Claude)* Each of the six pilots has the head of their own standing repair crew: six lesser people who may grow into bigger, more interesting roles later. The crews also maintain the pilot's vehicle alongside the Frame, competing for the same technician-day allocation, and they answer to Hulda Brack. Names, personalities and how each relates to their pilot are open. — known some · told later · source D075

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `directorate-posts.range-safety-officer-his-call-is-not-arguable` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The Range Safety Officer's call on a machine or a pilot is final. Arguing with it is the single thing that will get a trainee pulled off the ground, and it is not personal when it happens. He will explain his criteria in full, patiently, to anybody who asks before their run. Nobody ever asks before, and he has noticed. — known nobody · told later · source D075, D081

### The four founders *(group · 12 ink · 19 pencil · 1 open · 20 GM-only)*

`founders` · threads: The founders

**Notes.** How the names come out (D048): in play, not in Scene 0: in a history class or another event, with a skill roll, and perhaps in two places that each sell it from a different angle. Shucks's badge (MORDANT) and his "Yes, that one" at Intake Medicals now land before the players know the names; the history lesson can pay that off.

**What people know**

- `founders.four` *(Ink)* Four people founded the Directorate. — known everyone · told from the start · source D025, D048
- `founders.promise` *(Ink)* They promised that the next time, nobody would be caught unprepared, and founded the Directorate to keep that promise. — known everyone · told from the start · source D025, S001
- `founders.painting` *(Ink)* On Founding Day there is a painting of the four in some supporters' shop windows. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `founders.ribbon` *(Ink)* At least one of the founders might turn up to cut the ribbon at a major event. — known everyone · told from the start · source D048
- `founders.names` *(Ink)* The four are Hyuck, Rupiah, Anabala and Shucks Mordant. — known everyone · told Episode One · School: First Period · source D024, D026, D056
- `founders.pictures` *(Ink)* Every approved picture of the four shows four tall, handsome humans. — known everyone · told Episode One · School: First Period · source D027, D043, D056
- `founders.not-waved-about` *(Ink)* The city doesn't make a fuss of its founders being long-lived. It's faintly embarrassing, so nobody waves it in anyone's face. — known everyone · told Episode One · School: First Period · source D028, D058
- `founders.alive` *(Ink)* All four are alive. Three work on the base; Anabala is a free agent. — known some · told later · source D028
- `founders.charter-signatures` *(Ink)* The founding charter carries four signatures: a flowing hand, a quick doctor's scrawl, HYUCK in capitals pressed so hard the nib tore the paper, and small careful characters in a script nobody in Kurose reads. — known everyone · told Episode One · Assembly · source D044
- `founders.founding-day-anthem` *(Pencil · Claude)* Founding Day is the city's holiday for the founders, with Rupiah cutting the ribbon, as he has since the party's grandparents were children, and the anthem about the harbour. — known everyone · told later · source D071
- `founders.household-names` *(Pencil · Claude)* The four are household names in Kurose: children are named after them, and every school exam has a question on them. — known everyone · told later · source D074, D026
- `founders.page-forty` *(Pencil · Claude)* The school's approved history spends one page on First Impact, page forty, in the passive voice. It names all four as heroes and omits the cause and what they looked like, and its margin dates do not reconcile. It is not a lie anybody is currently telling: it is a two-hundred-year tidying that nobody alive has had reason to examine. — known some · told later · source D078, D022, D027

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `founders.what-they-were` *(Ink · GM-only)* The real four were a gnoll (Hyuck), an elf (Rupiah), a very small mitflit (Anabala) and a man who is now a skeleton (Shucks). — known few · told later · source D027, D043
- `founders.level` *(Ink · GM-only)* The four founders are level 15: impossibly powerful against a level-1 party. — known nobody · told later · source D047
- `founders.charter-hands` *(Ink · GM-only)* On the charter, the flowing hand is Rupiah's, the doctor's scrawl is Shucks's, the capitals are Hyuck's, and the small careful characters are Anabala's, in mitflit script. — known few · told later · source D044
- `founders.can-be-eclipsed` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* The party can, in the end, surpass the founders. — known nobody · told later · source D047, D070
- `founders.older-printing` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The school's approved history names all four as heroes and never says how the rift opened. Older printings in the back cupboard carry a memorial plate showing the four as they were, one very small and one not human; every later printing replaced it with a painting of four tall humans. — known few · told later · source D077, D022, D027
- `founders.the-tidying` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Nobody is keeping the founders' real faces secret. Two centuries of posters, statues-that-aren't and textbook editions made the four more heroic and more human with every printing, until the true account, four strange people who caused the thing they are famous for stopping, became the one version nobody would believe. — known nobody · told later · source D074, D027
- `founders.diplomacy-first` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* In their own time the four made peace with the mitflits instead of fighting them, and kept making peace where the story they were in expected a fight: their first sessions of the old campaign, in the town of Otari beside the ruined Gauntlight Keep, bent away from the script because diplomacy won through, and they later brokered peace between Otari and the mitflits. — known few · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029
- `founders.the-inquisitors` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Soon after the four took to the town of Otari, Inquisitors of Abadar, god of law and money, in blood-red cloaks and led by Inquisitor Sofie Reitz, with Kanika, Halina Benchae, Bronwen Rodford, Laurette Piraudrt, Zibene and Anja Blairr, came asking questions about the mitflits at the keep. They became allies, and the four kept their friendship with Reitz through the hunters, the nuns and the portal. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029
- `founders.the-nuns` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Hunters killed a gnoll and took a party of Abadar's nuns prisoner for witnessing it, and a mage, Regina Key, wiped the nuns' memories on William Charles Baldwin's orders. One nun, Esther, escaped and led the four to the hunters' camp. Regina was arrested with the camp, and the nuns' memories never fully came back. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029, D031
- `founders.the-horse` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The four crossed the hunters over a horse: Hyuck coveted one of theirs, paid a thief to steal it, and had the hide made into armour, the Barding of Vengeance. It is the "horse's leather" Baldwin later accuses them over. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029
- `founders.three-forts` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* With the keep overcrowded and Otari uneasy, the mitflits' council sent the four to look at three ruined forts as a new home: Fort Ranhold, Fort Croglang and Stonehill Keep. At Ranhold they found insect tunnels and an ooze that had killed the mitflits who had settled it in 4700. At Croglang they found Baldwin Manor, once Croglang Castle, where the four rescued mitflits forced to make weapons, fought through the manor with the Inquisitors beside them, and crossed the Shadow Plane and Abadar's Plane of Order in a single night. Baldwin accused them of killing his family. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029, D031, D081
- `founders.as-they-were` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* In their adventuring days the four were a gnoll barbarian who talked to his ancestors (Hyuck), a skeleton rogue with a doctor's hands (Shucks), a mitflit who brokered pacts (Anabala) and an elf oracle of the stars who had trained as a performer (Rupiah). The others could be unsure what to make of each other: early on Rupiah worried about wandering into the wild with a skeleton, a strange robot and a gnoll. — known few · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029
- `founders.a-week` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The end of the four's adventuring days went fast: from Volkheed and Baldwin Manor, through the jungle ship and First Impact, to Nirvana took them only about a week, in midsummer 4721 AR. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D030, D031
- `founders.the-plea` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* On the generation ship's cargo deck, as the breach opened, a mitflit council leader, Comhphas, sent the four a plea: the mitflits at Gauntlight were outnumbered by hunters with dark magic and were building a counterpart portal, and "time behaves differently there; you'll emerge just in time to make a difference." The four went through, and came out in Nirvana, where Sarenrae received them in Luminara, a golden city of light with a cathedral at its heart. She told them they had come "through an act not born of intent but of consequence", named them, and set them to mend the tear they had made themselves, as a chance for redemption, promising to return them afterwards. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D030, D032, D040, D081
- `founders.the-others` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Others travelled with the four for a time: Djarvik, a gnoll sorcerer, joined before Nirvana; Sniffy Snout, a bloodhound-shoony swashbuckler, for the jungle and the ship; Dave, Hyuck's familiar, who was, one session, "a traitor"; a ratfolk gunslinger Inquisitor, Mr Snuggly Wuffles, whose business card all four carried; and Sister Syntax, an android cleric who stood in for a night. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029
- `founders.the-contract` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* A letter in a flowery, elaborate hand, signed "[Elusive Quill]", hired an assassin, Peregrine, "Harbinger of Moonlit Silhouettes and Hushed Laments", to give "eternal repose" to four accidental trespassers on a plan: a beast with a sunlit face and dark coat, a phantasm stitched from obsidian edges, a disciple of hushed echoes, and an enigma in unassuming garments. It describes the four, and who sent it is not recorded. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029
- `founders.old-campaign-closure` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Blank Inheritance is an attempt to tie everything up at once: it gives closure to the original adventure, which was never finished and stopped with the four on a different plane, Nirvana, while also being a new campaign in its own right. The old material is source, not a straitjacket, and may be rewritten, enhanced or clarified wherever this one needs it. — known nobody · told later · source D078, D030

Told in the plan: Chapter 11 (`founders.never-knew-the-watcher`); Chapter 12 (`founders.pictures-are-the-lie`).

`hanabusa-booking-office`

### The Kurose Police *(group · 4 pencil · 1 GM-only)*

`kurose-police` · threads: The mayor and the police

**Notes.** The mayor makes the two work together on raids against organised criminals and dangerous cultists, and they do it uneasily (`mayor.support-forces-cooperation`, D068). Everywhere else the distrust stands.

**What people know**

- `kurose-police.distrust-directorate` *(Pencil · hers)* The police and the Directorate aren't good allies: they distrust each other. What happens with the police doesn't reach the Directorate quickly or clearly, if at all. — known some · told later · source D035, D070, D081
- `kurose-police.jurisdiction-quarrel` *(Pencil · Claude)* The quarrel between the police and the Directorate is jurisdiction: the Directorate takes anything alien, the police take everything else, and every incident with both in it is split down the middle and never stitched back together. The police work beside the Directorate on raids because the mayor makes them, and they don't like it. Ask them for anything else and you get nowhere quickly: sharing a raid isn't sharing a file. — known some · told later · source D071, D035, D068, D074, D081

Told in the plan: Chapter 2 (`kurose-police.break-up-demonstrations`); Chapter 11 (`kurose-police.the-file`).

### The mitflits *(group · 22 pencil · 1 open · 10 GM-only)*

`mitflits` · threads: The mitflits and the gathering

**What people know**

- `mitflits.wild` *(Pencil · Claude)* The mitflits of Golarion are small, goblin-like, cute and a nuisance: the "wild" mitflits, the only kind on Golarion, living around the city and the hangars. They have never been hunted, bountied, exterminated or treated as vermin at any point in this world's history; at worst they are a nuisance, and thought rude. — known everyone · told later · source D071, D015, D072, D014, D081
- `mitflits.look` *(Pencil · hers)* Wild mitflits are blue-skinned elfin goblin people, quite goblinoid, but cute rather than gruesome, with bright, intelligent eyes. High mitflits look like high-fantasy elves with blue skin: elegant, androgynous, unblemished and aloof, plainly a star-faring people. Nobody on Golarion looks like that now. — known some · told later · source D072, D015, D031
- `mitflits.helpful` *(Pencil · hers)* Mitflits have a horrible characteristic: they are extremely helpful when given the right tasks, and fascinated by the production of technology. It is what makes them so easy to use. It is a people's virtue that others exploit, never servility. — known some · told later · source D072, D032
- `mitflits.rude` *(Pencil · hers)* Mitflits annoy people the way a rude goblinoid with little respect for authority would in a 1950s Japanese city: they don't keep the same traditions, and they are weird outsiders. They skip the forms, ignore seniority and address people wrongly. The offence is social, never criminal. — known everyone · told later · source D072, D015
- `mitflits.rare-at-first` *(Pencil · Claude)* At the start of the campaign mitflits are extremely rare in Kurose. They grow steadily commoner, not because more are born or move in for ordinary reasons, but because they are gathering on purpose, to all be in one place when they leave to go home. — known everyone · told later · source D072
- `mitflits.young-pilots` *(Pencil · hers)* Some young mitflits volunteer to fight using the machines, and some mitflits find that abhorrent. Many mitflit communities are essentially pacifist, but the younger members of the clans are their own spirits, and willing to fight to protect the city directly. — known some · told later · source D072, D015
- `mitflits.freedom` *(Pencil · Claude)* Freedom is the mitflits' defining characteristic, and it applies internally: they will never vote as a bloc. Their history is brilliant minds with no social armour, talked into inventing weapons for a greedy lord who grew rich on it, and their split is generational. The elders remember the lord's workshop and know exactly what happens when someone finds their minds useful, so they refuse, and go to extremes for pacifism. The young do not remember: they see a magnificent machine and a city that needs them, and volunteer eagerly, walking into the identical trap wearing a uniform. — known some · told later · source D078, D081
- `mitflits.wont-explain` *(Pencil · Claude)* Mitflits will not explain themselves. Discussing mitflit technology falls under the same social taboo the city applies to magic: wise to conceal, vulgar to flaunt. Pressed, Bobbin will note, without drama, that mitflit technology is many times more powerful than terrestrial magic, because magic is slowly draining from Golarion. — known some · told later · source D078
- `mitflits.dont-know-gen-2` *(Pencil · hers)* Wild mitflits are uncomfortable around Gen 2 Frames, but it is important that the mitflits do not instantly understand where Gen 2 comes from. — known some · told later · source D078, D034

**Secrets: only a few, or nobody, know** *(GM-only)*

- `mitflits.descended-from-crew` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The mitflits are descended from the generation ship's crew. — known few · told later · source D071, D007, D031
- `mitflits.feel-the-watcher` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* The mitflits feel the Watcher in the air as something godlike and comforting that keeps them going the right way. "The Observer" is their old word for that presence. None of them knows it's real, or what it is. — known few · told later · source D071, D040
- `mitflits.degraded` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* The generation ship's crew were alien and robotic. Over the ages since the crash their descendants dispersed and forgot their skills, and became weaker, more primitive and more violent: the real reason they are thought "the least of races". Small communities of mitflits survived and kept alive the old ways and the older memories, and that surviving thread of memory is what makes a return home possible. They are wild mitflits like the rest: what they kept is memory, not looks. — known few · told later · source D072, D007, D031, D081
- `mitflits.keen` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* Many mitflits wouldn't be ready to hear, or believe, that they came from beyond the stars. All of them will be keen for the adventure, though: they are not a tragic people guarding a sad secret. — known few · told later · source D072, D015
- `mitflits.gauntlight` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* Two hundred years ago the four founders befriended a band of mitflits whom everyone else treated as a nuisance or as savants to be owned, gave them a home in Gauntlight Keep, and helped them build a government, with Anabala in charge. — known few · told later · when 4721 AR · source D072, D029
- `mitflits.gauntlight-council` *(Pencil · Claude · GM-only)* At Gauntlight Keep the mitflits took charge in a spirited first meeting; once the rules of meetings were explained they took to them with alacrity, and when they learned they could "vote" by ayes and nays it became bedlam, but the shape of a society started to develop. The council's leaders were Comhphas, Scrawng and Anabala, in a triumvirate, and a busy mitflit marketplace grew in the keep under Miriq the Magnificent. — known nobody · told later · when 4721 AR · source D074, D029
- `mitflits.muddled` *(Pencil · hers · GM-only)* To Ingram's mind the mitflits were star-faring robots originally, but their biology, magic and cybernetics all became muddled on Golarion over the thousands of years. They became a joke, the least of races. — known nobody · told later · source D078, D006

Told in the plan: Chapter 5 (`mitflits.avoid-gen-2`); Chapter 6 (`mitflits.the-gathering`, `mitflits.going-missing`); Chapter 13 (`mitflits.split`); Chapter 16 (`mitflits.politics-aboard`); Chapter 18 (`mitflits.high-mitflits`).

Still hers: `mitflits.what-the-wild-find`.

### The night regulars *(group · 38 pencil)*

`night-regulars`

**What people know**

- `night-regulars.aucourt` *(Pencil · Claude)* Basile Aucourt (Kalo): Long-stay patient, Ward Four, the General Hospital, a harbour pilot from Taldor, on the far side of the world. A long-stay patient with a leg in traction, in a contraption of pulleys he complains about constantly. Courtly, theatrical and a little too grand, in a Minkai he learned over ships' radios. Calls the ward 'the ship', the nurse 'the captain', and the other patients 'passengers', his opening line to anyone new is 'Ah, new passengers. Welcome aboard. The captain is at the far end, and she runs a very tight ship.' He tells the time by the tide rather than the clock, and still wakes for the four o'clock high water out of thirty years' habit, even though the rest of him can't act on it. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.chiyo` *(Pencil · Claude)* Chiyo Nakamura (Human): Second-term candidate from a fishing village, has never won a hand. A second-year candidate from a fishing village up the coast, with round cheeks, a scrap of blue cloth tying back her hair and her sleeves rolled to the elbow, who has not yet won a single hand of Last Ferry. She smiles the moment she picks up a good hand, knows she is doing it, and cannot stop; she counts her chores on her fingers. Warm and bright and a little breathless, and she apologises when she wins an argument. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.daisuke` *(Pencil · Claude)* Daisuke Kanno (Human): Stagehand, doorman and lantern-keeper for the Oddwater Company. The Oddwater Company's stagehand, doorman and lantern-keeper: a broad young man in a canvas apron with a cap pulled low, who puts a hand on something solid before he starts any job, as if the floor might argue. He calls Tamsin 'the boss' and never by her name. Short and dry, with a laugh he tries to keep in. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.faruq` *(Pencil · Claude)* Faruq Sallah (Pahtra): Candidate from Katapesh, harmonica player. A quiet young pahtra from Katapesh, far across the sea: short tawny fur, tall ears, a candidate's tunic worn under a maroon wool scarf that is the loudest thing on the roof. He plays the harmonica and says very little, tapping it against his palm before he plays, and answering a question he dislikes with two notes, going down. Soft, few words, very dry. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.gennai` *(Pencil · Claude)* Gennai: Night porter, the General Hospital. The night porter, pushing the tea trolley down Ward Four squeaking on its wheels, as he has every night for longer than anyone remembers. Pours for whoever is awake, and talks while he pours. Old, long-serving, quietly one of the better-informed people on the island without meaning to be, porters and nurses hear what the hospital is told to make ready for before anyone else does, and Gennai in particular knows how many beds and when, though never what for. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.genzo` *(Pencil · Claude)* Genzō Amemiya (Ysoki): Night observer, the Met Office. The night observer of the Met Office: a small, grey-whiskered ysoki in an oilskin coat and sou'wester who has kept the night watch for twenty years and speaks to his instruments in the same gentle voice he uses on people. He marks each hour by knocking it out on the brass rail with one knuckle, one knock for each hour, and only then says the number, and he taps the glass of the barometer and says good evening to it. Old-fashioned, gentle and precise, with a sailor's habits. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.grenna` *(Pencil · Claude)* Grenna Hollowmark (Dwarf): Dwarf candidate in the next room, who snores. A short, broad, ruddy first-term candidate with two thick braids and a square jaw, who lives in the next room and snores through the plywood wall like a sawmill, and whom everyone forgives. She raps her knuckles on any piece of wood before she trusts it, and handles anything broken like a patient: gently, and talking to it quietly. Cheerful, practical, and louder than she means to be. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.hachi` *(Pencil · Claude)* Hachirō Mase (Dwarf): Retired Frame fitter, bucket number four, the Bathhouse. A small, round, bald dwarf with a great white moustache and forty years of grease worked into the creases of his hands, who sits in the steam with a folded towel on his head and his own bucket beside him, number four. He talks about Frames the way old men talk about horses they have known, and about the pilots who drove them as somebody else's children. His stories take the long way round: he holds up one finger when the good part is coming, and then does not reach it for a while. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.hana` *(Pencil · Claude)* Hana Kurogane (Gnome): Second-term candidate, keeper of the notebook. A small second-year candidate with big bright eyes, her hair wrapped in a scarf and a dressing gown over her tunic, who keeps a fat notebook of everything she has been told and taps her pencil against her teeth while she decides how much of it to believe. She never repeats a rumour without saying who told her and how far she trusts them. Fast, delighted, and precise about her sources. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.haru` *(Pencil · Claude)* Haru Ishikawa (Android): First-term candidate, in the group's room. A first-term candidate a long way from home: slight and pale, with the faint seam lines at the temple and jaw that mark him as an android, a tunic a size too big for him and a folded letter he keeps taking out and putting away. Quiet, polite and a little formal, he brings up home the way people press a bruise, mostly by accident, and then looks embarrassed. He apologises to furniture when he bumps into it, and he is funniest when he forgets to be nervous. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.imai` *(Pencil · Claude)* Setsuko Imai (Ysoki): Long-stay patient, Ward Four, the General Hospital, formerly ran the island's telephone exchange for thirty-one years. A long-stay patient on Ward Four with a mending hip, in the bed next to the soldier. Ran the island's telephone exchange for thirty-one years before her hip put her here, every call on the island went through her board, and she still knows a voice before it gives its name, in her sleep. Bright, fast and nosy, with an operator's crisp manners when she remembers them. Knits without looking at her needles, and points with them instead of her finger. Opens on any newcomer at once: 'New ones! Come here where I can see you. What have they done to you, and who's your mother?' — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.isamu` *(Pencil · Claude)* Isamu Hamada (Orc): Block warden of Row E, retired tug skipper. The block warden of Row E and a retired tug skipper: a big grey-stubbled orc with small worn tusks, a peaked cap and a heavy pea coat, who has never once seen anybody on his roof. He talks to the ceiling when he is saying something he shouldn't, and addresses every candidate as if they were a visiting officer, however young. Gruff, loud, slow, and nowhere near as stern as he would like to be. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.joji` *(Pencil · Claude)* Joji Mabuchi (Goblin): Pit hand, the oldest on the night crew. The oldest pit hand on the night crew: a grey-green goblin with big drooping ears, grease in every crease and a rag over one shoulder, who sucks his teeth before he disagrees with anything and talks to the Frame's leg as if it could hear him. Slow, gravelly and grumbling, with a joke hidden inside every second complaint. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.kaede` *(Pencil · Claude)* Kaede Ishimori (Elf): Night foreman, No. 1 Machine Shop. The night foreman of No. 1 Machine Shop: a tall elf woman in teal-grey overalls with her hair pinned tight, a clipboard held to her chest and a pencil that taps twice on it before she says anything important. Calm, exact and a little dry, she speaks in instructions and means them kindly, and she directs the shop by station rather than by name, so that everyone hears their own job called back at them. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.kazue` *(Pencil · Claude)* Kazue Tsurumi (Vesk): Attendant, the Bathhouse. A tall, broad-shouldered Vesk woman with dark green scales and a jaw like a ship's prow, who sits on a high wooden seat at the door in a white sailor's cap and a navy smock with the sleeves rolled. A brass whistle hangs at her collar, and when she lifts it the whole bathhouse goes quiet. She runs the place the way she once ran a ship's deck: lockers numbered like cabins, the water's heat chalked up every hour, and a rule for everything that she will explain exactly once. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.kiku` *(Pencil · Claude)* Kiku Enomoto (Dwarf): Keeper, the Paper Lantern. Keeper of the Paper Lantern, a civilian izakaya off Directorate ground in Kurose's entertainment quarter. Stout, sharp-eyed and fast behind the counter, she runs the place on one rule: rank doesn't matter past the noren curtain, and she enforces it on everyone equally, dock hand and off-duty candidate alike. Warm underneath, dry on top, never wastes a word. Wipes the counter when she's deciding what to say, and counts a table by heads before she pours, and has never once got a tab wrong. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.kuroki` *(Pencil · Claude)* Shuhei Kuroki (Orc): Private, Minkai army city garrison, a patient in the next bed, the General Hospital. A young soldier of Minkai's army, city garrison, brought over from the causeway gate this afternoon with his wrist in fresh plaster. His army tunic is folded on the chair, and there's a bag of oranges on his locker that he hasn't touched. Guarded and angry, not ashamed, angry. The moment he sees the party's Directorate kit on their own chairs, he says flatly, 'You're theirs, then,' and turns his back. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.lucan` *(Pencil · Claude)* Lucan Farrow (Halfling): Second-term candidate from Absalom, cardsharp. A small, quick second-year candidate from Absalom, with a rakish grin, the uniform tunic hanging open over a mustard-yellow silk waistcoat, and a coin that walks across his knuckles while he thinks. He is the loudest thing at the table and he cheats, cheerfully and well, and he gets more generous the closer he is to doing it: the drinks are on him, the good seat is yours. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.michiru` *(Pencil · Claude)* Michiru Arai (Human): Third-term candidate, dealer and keeper of the debt board. A third-year candidate with a neat bob, a stub of chalk between two fingers and the slate-grey tunic buttoned to the collar, who deals the game and keeps the debt board with the calm of a court clerk who enjoys the job more than she admits. She writes on the board while she talks and never looks at it, and she does not raise her voice: a rule is a rule because it is up there in her handwriting. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.mira` *(Pencil · Claude)* Mira Kostel (Brenneri): Switchboard operator on the island's night exchange. A switchboard operator on the island's night exchange: a sleek, brown-furred brenneri with long whiskers that twitch when she catches someone's mood, a cardigan over her blouse and a dent above one ear where the headset sits, which she rubs when she is tired. She introduces people by patching them together, a hand on each elbow, a small pause, and then they are talking. Quick, warm and a little breathless, with a foreigner's careful Minkai and a laugh at the end of most sentences. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.mori` *(Pencil · Claude)* Aiko Mori: Cleaner, the General Hospital, contracted through a firm from the city. A young cleaner working the sluice room late at night, one hand held stiffly, favouring it without ever quite stopping, and hoping nobody notices. She cut it on a broken bottle and it wants proper attention, but she's not asking for any. The cleaning went out this year to a firm from the city, and the firm sends home anyone hurt on shift and doesn't have them back, she has a little brother to feed, which she never offers as a reason, it's just why she's still working. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.morishita` *(Pencil · Claude)* Mrs Fumiko Morishita (Human): Block warden, Row C Block 3. The block warden of Row C, Block 3: a woman of sixty or so with grey hair pinned up, round spectacles, a lumpy hand-knitted cardigan over a housedress and felt slippers, who counts everyone in at night with a torch she points politely at the ceiling, never at a face, because that would be rude. She asks for lights out rather than ordering it, and thanks the room when it complies. Brisk and proper, and then kind by accident when she thinks nobody is watching. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.mrs-handa` *(Pencil · Claude)* Mrs Chiyoko Handa (Human): Keeps the pickle stall in the Market Hall, front row at every show. Keeps the pickle stall in the Market Hall and has the front-row seat at every show: a small, brisk woman with her hair in a tight bun, a floral apron over a cardigan, and a jar of pickles usually tucked under one arm. She draws herself up an inch before she tells anyone off, so you always get a moment to reconsider, and she pats the arm of whoever she is talking to. Fond and bossy, and she talks to the young as if they were her grandchildren whether they are or not. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.mrs-ueda` *(Pencil · Claude)* Mrs. Ueda (Halfling): The block's night warden, Row B Block 8. The night warden of Row B, Block 8: a tiny, round old halfling woman with white hair in curlers under a headscarf and a quilted dressing gown, carrying a torch like a candle. She is so gentle with everybody that it takes a while to notice she is counting them, and she knocks twice on the door before she comes in, and never on anything else. Slow, amused and unimpressed. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.nadi` *(Pencil · Claude)* Nadi Obasi (Human): The observer's assistant, eighteen. The observer's assistant: eighteen, quick and practical, with a pencil always in her hand, chalk dust on her fingers, a grey work smock and a raised eyebrow. She chalks the numbers on the board and corrects anyone's arithmetic, her own included, out loud. She thinks in numbers, and has a sharp sense of humour. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.nkiru` *(Pencil · Claude)* Nkiru Oduya (Skittermander): Gantry-crane driver, who sings the lifts. The gantry-crane driver: a six-armed skittermander with bright orange fur, a leather cap with the goggles pushed up, and a cab arranged so that every lever is under one hand or another. She hums the next lift before she starts it and sings the lifts down across the shop floor, and she names people from twenty metres up by whatever she can see of them: a hat, a height, a limp. Big, bright and easy, shouted down from the roof. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.obi` *(Pencil · Claude)* Obiajulu Eze (Elf): Second-term candidate from far away, checks every rumour. A tall, thin second-year candidate from very far away, in round spectacles and the slate tunic, who checks every rumour the room produces and is very nearly always wrong. He counts his points off on his fingers, is at his most certain a moment before he turns out to be mistaken, and is quick to get excited and quick to be let down. Earnest and precise. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.petr` *(Pencil · Claude)* Petr Vasko (Orc): Welder, singer, the room's friend. A huge, warm orc welder with a broad friendly face, small tusks, a leather cap pushed back and a scorch-marked apron, who is the room's friend and its worst singer. He takes a breath like a man about to dive before every story, and the room leans in. Big, warm, loud, full of stories that wander. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.ren` *(Pencil · Claude)* Ren Saeki (Halfling): Apprentice fitter, nineteen, the youngest in the crews. The youngest in the crews: a nineteen-year-old halfling apprentice fitter in patched teal overalls, oil to the elbows, a stripe of orange paint on his cap and the look of somebody trying very hard to sound older. He wipes his hands on his overalls when he is nervous and picks his words carefully, as if he might be marked on them. Quick and eager. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.sanzo` *(Pencil · Claude)* Sanzo (Goblin): Wandering musician and storyteller, the Paper Lantern. A wandering musician and storyteller who's been drifting through Kurose for years, and always seems to circle back to the Paper Lantern's counter. Small, wiry, and never quite still, he plays a battered shamisen badly and with complete commitment, and tells stories that are half true and impossible to sort from the half that isn't. Warm, theatrical, always slightly performing even when he isn't trying to. Starts a true story exactly the same way he starts a false one, and tunes the shamisen between sentences whether or not it needs it. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.sayo` *(Pencil · Claude)* Sayo Iwamura (Human): Second-term candidate, stargazer. A second-term candidate and stargazer with a homemade chart of the autumn sky, a borrowed greatcoat over her tunic and a pencil behind her ear, who counts the stars off on her fingers as she names them. She talks about stars the way other people talk about relatives, with strong opinions and no doubt at all. Quick, precise, a little bossy, and very kind underneath it. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.sigrun` *(Pencil · Claude)* Sigrun Halvard (Ikeshti): Crane driver, champion of the hottest pool, the Bathhouse. A small, stocky Ikeshti woman with hard red scales, bright orange eyes and a grin that shows a few small teeth. She drives a crane on the quays by day and holds the record for the hottest pool in the bathhouse by night: she sinks into water that sends everyone else out and looks faintly let down by the temperature, and when she laughs she slaps the surface hard enough to wet the row behind her. Loud, blunt and cheerful, in short strong sentences. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.tama` *(Pencil · Claude)* Tama (Leshy): Waitress, the Paper Lantern. The youngest regular at the Paper Lantern, and its waitress since she was old enough to carry a tray. Small, leafy-haired and wide-eyed, she is quick, eager, and always asking a second question before the first one's been answered. She has never once been past the checkpoint onto Directorate ground, let alone off the island, and she asks the candidates who come in everything about the world past it without quite meaning to pry. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.tamsin` *(Pencil · Claude)* Tamsin Oddwater (Gnome): Illusionist, head of the Oddwater Company. The illusionist at the head of the Oddwater Company: a small, warm-faced gnome woman with wild silver curls under a violet velvet top hat and a coat lined with stars. On stage she is huge and warm; off it she is quick, plain and funny, like somebody's favourite aunt. She greets a town by name like an old friend she is slightly worried about, and asks a question and answers it herself before anyone else can. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.tokuji` *(Pencil · Claude)* Tokuji Tsuruta (Human): Keeper of the shrine. The keeper of the shrine, seventy-eight years old, deeply lined, in a padded indigo coat, who sweeps the paving every night and has done for sixty years. He leans on his broom before he says anything he thinks is important, and talks to the shrine cat as if the cat were in charge. Slow, dry and old-town plain: he says exactly what he means and not a word more. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.tomoe` *(Pencil · Claude)* Tomoe Hashida (Human): Chief of Refit Crew Three, keeper of the slate. The chief of Refit Crew Three, who keeps the chalk slate behind the bar: a woman in her forties with cropped hair, teal-grey overalls with the crew number stencilled in orange, and tally marks in chalk on her sleeve. She taps the slate with the chalk when she makes a point, and knows everyone by crew before she knows their name; anyone without one is simply a candidate until proven otherwise. Short, dry, never unkind, and she counts everything. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.tsubaki` *(Pencil · Claude)* Haruko Tsubaki: Night sister, Ward Four, the General Hospital. Night sister of Ward Four at the General Hospital, a department store once, and the ward still carries the old brass sign for Gentlemen's Outfitting over its door. After dark, she is the ward's real boss. Brisk and low-voiced, a night voice that carries further than a shout, kind underneath and never in a hurry to show it. Calls every patient by their bed number until she likes them, and 'dear' once she does; taps the watch pinned to her apron when she wants someone to stop talking. Twenty-two years on nights. She has done the evening paper's crossword every night for twenty of them and has never finished one, she reads the clues aloud to anybody still awake. Runs a tight ward (lights out at ten, rounds at two) and nobody dies on it if she can help it, and she usually can. — known some · told later · source D075
- `night-regulars.technical-track-student` *(Pencil · Claude)* The technical-track student (Talphi): Technical-track student at the Canteen, easier to talk to. A young Talphi, small and soft-furred, with a pink snub nose, tiny kind eyes behind thick round spectacles and broad clever hands, sitting back in a chair with the sleeves of a technical-track uniform rolled and the tunic hung over the chair behind. Quiet, warm and unhurried, the easiest person in the room to end up next to. Asks a real follow-up question instead of talking about themself, and is honest, a little tired, and not glamorous about what repair crew work is actually like: mostly waiting for the part to actually break. — known some · told later · source D075
