**D081 · Merge wave 1: pieces of one thing become one thing**

- anabala (anabala.wakes-the-ship, anabala.way-home): wakes-the-ship (pencil) has Anabala wake the search ship in Chapter 14 to take her people home, so that it lifts in Chapter 15; the open decision anabala.way-home still asks whether her way home is the search ship under Kurose or the shuttle under Kortos.
- anabala (anabala.recruited-the-four, mitflits.gauntlight): recruited-the-four has Anabala, already one of the four, bring Hyuck, Shucks and Rupiah to intervene against Baldwin; mitflits.gauntlight has the four founders befriending a band of mitflits at Gauntlight Keep, with Anabala put in charge of their government afterwards. The two tellings of how the four and the mitflits came together do not fit.
- baldwin-manor (baldwin-manor.volkheed, baldwin-manor.mitflit-clan): volkheed says Inicrium mining began at Volkheed around 4171 AR; mitflit-clan has a clan arriving in 4147 AR and lending its skills to the Inicrium trade, twenty-four years before the mining began (unless the 'trade' is older than the mining).
- baldwin-manor (baldwin-manor.croglang): This one fact contradicts itself, as it admits: the old history has the castle built in 4221 AR and renamed in 4201 AR, twenty years before it was built.
- baldwin (baldwin.alive, anabala.knows-baldwin-lives): baldwin.alive ends 'Nobody knows' (known: nobody), which settles in advance what the open anabala.knows-baldwin-lives still asks (candidates: she knows, or she doesn't); baldwin.nobu-knows is the same question for Nobu and the Fixer.
- cicada (cicada.not-the-first-fight, the-soldier.the-squad): not-the-first-fight (told Chapter 9) calls the column raid 'the first real Cadre fight', while the-soldier.the-squad and the-soldier.never-kills (told Chapter 3) and the plan (beat--meet-the-cadre) have the party meet and fight an armed Cadre squad in Chapter 3; they agree only if 'real' means a fight where the Cadre fights to kill, as column.cadre-defends says of Chapter 9.
- cicada (cicada.witness-is-the-goal, cicada.nobody-dies): witness-is-the-goal says some of what Cicada does is 'now and then fatal in its consequences', while nobody-dies (and the-soldier.keeps-the-count-at-zero) say nobody has died at a demonstration; they agree only if 'what they do' means more than the demonstrations (the Cadre's work, the heists).
- cicada (cicada.no-leader-in-the-file, cicada.dangerous-cultists): no-leader-in-the-file says nobody in the Directorate is assigned to Cicada and its file holds only private showings, a mark or two and the odd arrest for a public nuisance, while dangerous-cultists (and the mayor's joint-raid arrangement, and the armed Cadre squad the party meets in Chapter 3) have the Directorate raiding 'dangerous cultists' beside the police; they fit only if the raids are never tied to a file.
- comms-officer (comms-officer.afraid-for-them, hulda-brack.no-secrets): afraid-for-them calls her the first adult in the campaign whose instinct is to protect the party; hulda-brack.no-secrets (Brack uses the machinery for them) and directorate.decent-adults (Shucks, Nobu and Taka are warm and on the children's side) already put kind adults in Episode One. Whether 'first' means the first to put herself between them and danger is for Ingram. A soft tension, not a flat contradiction.
- directorate (directorate.two-ends, directorate.first-look-mix): Both are Ingram's words. two-ends says the school and the base are one island with two ends, 'not one blended site', with the arrival end (causeway, Roadgate, hangar, checkpoints) pure military; first-look-mix says that on first arrival the campus reads as a genuine mix of military and school with neither dominating. Possibly reconcilable (a first look from the causeway taking in both ends), but each seems to deny the other until she says how.
- directorate (directorate.reads-the-messages, directorate.consent-in-the-forms): reads-the-messages puts the consent in a clause of FORM 1-B, the Service Agreement signed at induction; consent-in-the-forms puts it in the intake paperwork, 'the same forms' that ask for mother's maiden name twice, which directorate.form-12b (decided) says is Form 12-B, the intake screening form. Either they are two different forms or one fact has two homes.
- envoy (envoy.first-hello, envoy.swarm-felt-nothing, hori.peril): first-hello dates the Envoy 'about 15 years ago | about 1 year ago' (the open decision cicada.envoy-when), while swarm-felt-nothing says about 15 years and hori.peril says 'fifteen years of guilt'.
- era (era.dug-up-not-invented, era.tech-trickle, era.electronics-source): dug-up-not-invented says the gate is hard yet ship technology 'still leaks outwards from Kortos' and the phones run on the ship-derived substrate, which pre-answers the open decisions era.tech-trickle (does it reach civilian life at all?) and era.electronics-source (the generation ship's leak, or the search ship?).
- founders (founders.pictures-are-the-lie, founders.page-forty, founders.the-tidying): pictures-are-the-lie calls the founders' official pictures 'the lie'; page-forty says the approved history is 'not a lie anybody is currently telling' and the-tidying says nobody is keeping the faces secret, only a two-century tidying. Whether the official portrayal is a lie or an unexamined tidying is her call.
- founders (founders.what-they-were, founders.as-they-were): Pencil against ink (the ink one would win): founders.what-they-were calls Shucks 'a man who is now a skeleton', which reads as a man who later became one, while as-they-were has him 'a skeleton rogue' in the old campaign's adventuring days, as do shucks.shuck-mord ('two hundred years ago Shucks was a skeleton rogue, tomb-born') and D043's memorial plate ('a skeleton'). Worth her correcting the ink wording if it is a slip.
- general-hospital (general-hospital.who-oversees-it, directorate-posts.hospital-chief-of-staff): who-oversees-it is an open question (Claude proposed Shucks Mordant; Ingram has not confirmed it; nobody in particular or someone else are live), but directorate-posts.hospital-chief-of-staff states as fact that the hospital nominally answers to Shucks Mordant as the Directorate's Chief Medical Officer, who is never there in person.
- hyuck (hyuck.statue-as-described, hyuck.statue-material): statue-pose says 'if the stone were flesh', which presumes stone, while the open decision hyuck.statue-material still asks whether the statue is stone or bronze.
- directorate-institution (idea--the-watchers-early-voice, idea--the-voice-changes): Both give the Watcher's later voice, but this one is a legalistic claim-filer who says 'Survive all of it, and I'm done', while the other (and the Voice drafted in world/watcher.md) is a calm observer, and the fact watcher.stays has it remain over Kurose whatever the party survives.
- misc-clues (idea--censored-papers, the-registry.typed-per-clearance): The idea has each document censored to a clearance, with the censor's cuts telling the reader something; the fact has every clearance level typed separately, 'never censored afterwards', so there are no cuts to read.
- misc-clues (idea--censored-papers, idea--the-charters-black-bar): Ingram cut a publicly censored paragraph of the charter as 'a secret that is flaunted'; censoring every Directorate paper in view is the same flaunting made standard.
- sweep-v4 (idea--nobody-has-to-die, idea--one-death-precisely-placed): The first says every death in the campaign is one a human caused, with no corpses on the enemy side; the second has an early Claimant kill a man by accident.
- the-mayor (idea--mayor-first-appearance, mayor.own-agent): The idea has the party learn which of the city and the mayor's own position the mayor protects first; Ingram's fact has the mayor protect both equally.
- manako (manako.disgraced, manako.disgraced-after-the-spill): Ink says he was expelled after a 'breakdown' at a science conference; the pencil spill piece says he lost his career 44 years ago after the lab spill (shucks.supervised-the-disgrace agrees), six years before the conference: which event is the disgrace?
- manako (manako.disgraced-after-the-spill, manako.the-papers-are-his, manako.checks-first): The discredited papers are a forty-year-old study 'from before his disgrace', and checks-first has him develop their technique after the failed demonstration, but the disgrace is placed 44 years ago, before all of that.
- mitflit-home-world (mitflit-home-world.why-ships-fall, mitflit-home-world.who-fells-ships): why-ships-fall has the derelicts' logs in Chapter 17 explain why ships fall; one candidate of the open who-fells-ships is that it is never explained in the campaign.
- mitflits (mitflits.wild, baldwin.the-hunters): never-vermin says mitflits have never been hunted at any point in this world's history (her confirmation, D014: 'never hunted, never bountied'); the Baldwin items have his hunters capturing mitflit savants for their minds, and an army of hunters set against the mitflits at Gauntlight, which by the word is hunting them.
- mitflits (mitflits.wild, kurose.small-signs): never-vermin says mitflits are never treated as vermin; kurose.small-signs has a hand-lettered notice asking anyone who spots a mitflit to report it to the Harbour Office and not handle it themselves, which reads as a pest notice.
- mitflits (mitflits.wild, mitflits.rare-at-first): wild has the wild mitflits living around the city and the hangars; rare-at-first has mitflits extremely rare in Kurose at the start of the campaign. How many are about, and since when, is not the same in the two.
- mitflits (mitflits.gauntlight, mitflits.gauntlight-council): gauntlight has the four helping the mitflits build a government 'with Anabala in charge'; gauntlight-council says the council was led by a triumvirate of Comhphas, Scrawng and Anabala.
- mother (mother.old-campaign, mother.met-by-the-four, generation-ship.mitflit-village): old-campaign puts the mitflit village inside the jungle ship; met-by-the-four and generation-ship.mitflit-village put it beside the generation ship (while generation-ship.inside has two mitflit quarters within the ship).
- nirvana (nirvana.the-relic, rift.sarenrae-sent): the-relic says Sarenrae gave the four a relic to seal the breach between planes; rift.sarenrae-sent (open) says what exactly she sent them back with to close Kortos is not decided.
- nobu (nobu.looks-away, nobu.hides-well): looks-away says he reads as a man compensating for something and will not meet your eye when generous; hides-well says he is never nervous, evasive or cagey and nothing in his manner gives his secret away. - noodle-stand-owner (noodle-stand-owner.proof-of-an-outside, rest--the-paper-lantern): proof-of-an-outside makes her the campaign's only civilian fixture the Directorate does not own, a place where nobody is anybody's section; the haunt scene The Paper Lantern (sited by Ingram on a real building of The Slope) is a civilian izakaya off Directorate ground where nobody's rank matters, run by Kiku Enomoto, who runs the place exactly her own way.
- rift (rift.the-fumble, founders.the-plea): the-fumble says a planar breach flung the four across the planes to Nirvana; founders.the-plea says Comhphas's plea reached them as the breach opened and they went through a counterpart portal and came out in Nirvana: flung by the breach, or went through on purpose?
- rupiah (rupiah.elf, founders.what-they-were): rupiah.elf has it known by everyone that Rupiah is an elf; founders.what-they-were (decided) has the real four, the elf included, known by few, and founders.pictures has every approved picture show four tall humans, which an elf who cuts the ribbon in person each Founding Day would give away.

- sap (sap.last-sample, manako.first-supplier): last-sample says Manako reverse-engineered everything from the one sample he took; manako.first-supplier says a fragment of the Watcher stayed near him and helped him work out how to make more Sap (they may both be true).
- sap (sap.inert-12, sap.catalogued-at-kortos, section-officer.the-transmission-chain): Three ages for one sample: inert-12 says it is about a century old; catalogued-at-kortos dates the first trace about 120 years ago; section-officer.the-transmission-chain has Manako handed a century-old sample about forty years ago, which would make it about 140 now (probably only rounding).
- school-history-teacher (school-history-teacher.taught-straight, school-history-teacher.two-teachers): taught-straight says a student comes out of his class having learned something true about how the island got here and leaves it a GM call whether he knows more; two-teachers (known by nobody, so also not mergeable) says the history syllabus is an approved text that has been edited without his knowing, so what he teaches is not simply true and he does not know more.
- school-natural-history-teacher (school-natural-history-teacher.true-answers, school-history-teacher.says-i-dont-know): true-answers makes her the only teacher in the building who will happily tell a class she doesn't know; school-history-teacher.says-i-dont-know has the history teacher say I don't know plainly with no embarrassment, as does the Episode One first-period scene (Ota 'says I don't know plainly and doesn't mind').
- section-officer (section-officer.not-dangerous, section-officer.the-drains): not-dangerous says Vetch cannot get the party hurt and the worst he can do is a tedious fortnight; the Episode One scenes have him order them down the storm drains on the first night, and Flood Tunnel Clearance makes that the first real fight (six giant centipedes).

- shinobu (shinobu.the-colony, shinobu.the-cell): the-colony says part of the Watcher lives in her, so she is held in its attention more or less continuously and not glimpsed occasionally; the-cell and watched-in-her-cell say the Watcher finds its way into her cell and call what it does visits. A tension, not a flat contradiction: both hold if the main swarm visits and the colony is always there.
- shucks (shucks.knows-the-marker, shucks.found-the-marker): knows-the-marker says Shucks has known what the marker means since the party's intake; found-the-marker says he found the marker years ago, going back through the notes of the original Gen 2 trial pilots when the programme nearly folded.
- shucks (shucks.the-hand-then, shucks.rand-the-earlier-man, shucks.hand-detached, shucks.old-handwriting): When the hand became its own creature: the-hand-then dates it to 4721 AR ('already a creature of its own in the old days') and rand-the-earlier-man says it detached 'before any of this'; hand-detached says only 'some while ago', after Shucks put it in a necromantic beam; and the ink fact shucks.old-handwriting has Rand writing in Shucks's handwriting from before the hand came off, so that anything the founders signed two hundred years ago (the charter) shows it. If it was already loose in 4721 AR, it is unclear how the charter (presumably signed at the Directorate's founding, about five years after First Impact) carries its handwriting.
- shucks (shucks.on-the-list, shucks.supervised-the-disgrace, shucks.knows-hes-a-target): Pencil against an open decision: on-the-list and supervised-the-disgrace state that Shucks supervised Manako's disgrace personally and may feel his conscience salved; the open decision knows-hes-a-target says it is not decided whether he remembers Manako at all or what his role actually was (a direct decision, or a signature on someone else's).
- taka (taka.a-year-ahead, episode-c1e1--canteen): a-year-ahead says Taka sends them off to the drains; in the Episode One canteen scene Vetch gives Section Nine the drains and Taka only gets the last word (wear the waders).
- taka (taka.old-drill-briefing, episode-c1e2--zero-six-hundred): old-drill-briefing has Taka brief the Frame drill the next morning (the morning after the first evening), but the chapter plan puts his 0600 scene and the Frame drill on Day 3, two mornings after the canteen. It may only mean the next morning after the night off.
- the-outer-sea-wall (the-outer-sea-wall.the-tide-decides, the-outer-sea-wall.nobody-comes): the-tide-decides says the walk out is dry only for about four hours either side of low water (a window of up to eight hours each tide); nobody-comes says nobody will see who is there for four hours twice a day (four hours each tide). Either 'four hours either side' means four hours in all, or the two windows are different lengths.
- the-rock (the-rock.on-the-surface, the-rock.nine-doors): on-the-surface says the south-east side is bare reinforced ground with a few low vents; nine-doors puts nine round metal doors, each several metres across and ringed in hazard paint, flush with the ground on that same south-east side. Possible tension (the doors may simply be unnoticed or shut by the 'some' who have seen it), for Ingram to settle.
- the-rock (the-rock.what-it-is, the-rock.nine-doors): what-it-is (merged above into secret-prison-and-laboratory) says The Rock is reached only by a tunnel from Central, 'with no door of its own'; nine-doors says nine round doors lie flush with the ground and open upward onto the cells. Probably cell hatches rather than ways in, but the wording clashes until someone says so.
- vermilion-block (vermilion-block.just-a-department, vermilion-block.what-the-reagents-are-for): just-a-department says the Block has nothing to do with the Watcher, the magic shows or the Kortos rift, while the open question what-the-reagents-are-for asks whether the silo stock connects to anything else in the campaign; the pencil fact would answer the open question before she has.
- watcher (watcher.mass-clock, watcher.hidden-numbers): mass-clock says to show the Mass Clock to the party once they understand Sap, while hidden-numbers says the Mass Clock's position is never confirmed to them; sap.gauge's 'a rough gauge, never an exact number' may reconcile them, but it is her call.
- watcher (watcher.why-eyes, watcher.drowning-instrument, watcher.shaped-by-manako): The first two say the Watcher's eyes and ears are a sensor's reflex to perceive harder; shaped-by-manako says it has eyes and ears because Manako wanted to be seen and heard (they may be two layers: the reflex first, his portrait later).
- watcher (watcher.stays, watcher.fate): stays calls the Watcher a 'perpetual threat' over Kurose after Second Impact, while fate (open) leaves its ending to be chosen (it disperses for good, becomes harmless, or is taken home); 'perpetual' may pre-empt that.
- watcher (watcher.native-to-the-phones, era.electronics-source): native-to-the-phones says the Directorate's own electronics are ship technology that leaked out of Kortos; era.electronics-source (open) leaves undecided whether they come from the Kortos leak or the search ship under Kurose.

## §19 The ideas

### Book I, rethought *(2 live · 10 adopted · 1 rejected)*

Claude's proposals for Book I around Ingram's three combat tracks (D084). She loved almost all of them (D085); the adopted ones now live in the plan, the facts and the new people.

- `idea--three-unknown-things` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The three things of Episode Two are puzzles, very hard together, each with its own way of moving and one weakness, and all made of nanomachines, which nobody knows yet. The Loom is a tall lattice of dark threads that hangs above the roofs and weaves a web between buildings; whatever touches a thread is bound; its knot is the weak point. The Bell is a smooth dome that drifts at head height, sings one low tone and rolls towards noise; engines and sirens make its shockwaves worse, so silence is the answer. The Tide is a low sheet of dark liquid that spreads along the road, then stands up into a wave that sweeps the tram; it flows round obstacles and is fought from high ground. Help is a dial: the harbour battery, Vermilion Block casters on the roofs, the duty lance, and last the Young One's combat Frame. — when chapter 1
- `idea--clues-in-the-haunts-and-manako` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Each rest from Episode One carries one road to a Book I clue, so whichever the players choose, the clues reach them: the night observer's barometer twitches before each contact; the bathhouse's retired fitter knows exactly where a Gen 1's joints fail; the card game's regulars know the Hanko Men; a Ward Four nurse is one of the Faithful. Manako is their kindest friend in the city, and once tells one of them to stay off a certain square on a certain afternoon, which turns out to be the afternoon of a demonstration: one odd clue for the player who suspects him, and nothing more. — when book i
- `idea--book-i-braided` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* Book I is one braided case. The three combat tracks are tied together by Cicada's chemical: the Faithful release it at demonstrations; the gangs move the cult's paint, venues, permits, crowds and crates and steal chemical stock under cover of the demonstrations; and the Watcher's children can only form where the chemical was released. Every fight on every track hands the party one piece of one picture, and the official line (cultists summon the things) fits everything they see until they can test it. Book I ends when they prove it wrong with their own eyes. — when book i — became `are-the-cultists-summoning-them`, `episode-c4e2--the-square`
- `idea--episode-one-retuned` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* Episode One keeps its shape and gains three changes. The Road In splits into six short solo scenes, one per player, each a way into Kurose with one check, something to learn and something planted. The Errand expects the players to guess that the bubble docket is a prank within seconds, says so out loud, and lets them choose how to beat it, with short optional stops that each have their own reward and none that sends them on. The jam in the flood tunnel becomes a stack of smuggled crates, a hint of the criminal side and nothing more. — when chapter 1 — became `old-town-drains.smuggled-crates`, `episode-c1e1--the-errand`, `episode-c1e1--way-in-ferry`
- `idea--episode-two-lead-in` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* Episode Two's lead-in. The Override is the mayor's initiative arriving without the mayor's name on it: an order from above Vetch's head naming the six. The Night Off puts them in the Paper Lantern while a gang leans on its keeper. Slack Water finds an old violet stencil under the sea wall's growth. Every scene before the exercise gives them someone in the city to like. — when chapter 1 — became `episode-c1e2--the-override`, `episode-c1e2--the-night-off`, `episode-c1e2--slack-water`
- `idea--first-contact-dilemma` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* The first real fight is built so that acting is the only sensible or heroic choice, and the players know the price. Vetch orders them to hold. The Comms Officer is unsure what the three things are, disagrees with him, tries the duty officer, the Deputy Director's office and the Plot Room supervisor, and cannot get a better answer quickly. She gives the party everything she has and orders nothing. A tram with forty people aboard has stopped between the three things and the old town, and the duty lance is twelve minutes out. Afterwards Vetch charges them, the Deputy Director's room is frightening, Doctor Mordant asks for a private word, and the episode ends in Hangar Two with their names still chalked on the board. — when chapter 1 — became `episode-c1e2--unidentified-contact`, `comms-officer.unsure-and-disagrees`
- `idea--g1-movers` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* The Watcher's next children, in Chapter 2, hunt whatever moves: trams, running crowds, machines on the move. Stillness hides you. The Faithful at the site stand still by doctrine and are spared, which looks like proof that the cult controls the creatures, so the official line gets stronger before it breaks. The fight is red light, green light at building scale. — when chapter 2 — became `beat--the-first-new-kind`, `episode-c2e1--the-fish-market`
- `idea--five-gangs` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* Five gangs, each with a flavour, a fight of its own and one service it sells the cult, so each raid yields a piece of one supply chain and every trail ends at the Hanabusa Booking Office. The Salt Dogs run the harbour by whistle and move the cult's crates. The Brass Choir fights to the tempo of a band that never stops, and rents Kiri her back rooms. The Hanko Men are polite forgers who burn their ledgers when raided, and sell permits for the marked squares. The Rust Saints are scrap salvagers in loader rigs welded from Frame parts, and repair weapons that no Golarion workshop could have made. The Sakura are hired crowds, in which paid civilians and real ones look alike, and fill the marked squares before a demonstration. — when book i — became `salt-dogs.who`, `brass-choir.who`, `hanko-men.who`, `rust-saints.who`, `the-sakura.who`
- `idea--cult-answers` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* How the cult answers the party's investigation, softest first. Persuade: Kiri's card goes to whichever of them Mrs. Ando saw on the way in. Obstruct: the Fixer has evidence disappear. Then fight: the Soldier's squad ambushes them to take evidence back, non-lethally, and calls them "Section Nine". Those the party takes alive are educated, competent and kind, the opposite of what the city assumes, and each gives up a small amount in debrief. — when chapter 3 — became `beat--cicada-notices-section-nine`, `beat--meet-the-cadre`, `beat--the-first-debrief`
- `idea--chapters-two-to-four` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* After Episode Two each chapter is a board of leads, not a script, with the Plot Room's calls arriving on the Watcher's clock and the players choosing the order of everything else. — when book i — became `episode-c2e1--the-case-board`, `episode-c3e1--the-case-board`, `episode-c4e1--the-case-board`
- `idea--book-i-last-day` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* Book I's last day. The violet marks, the booking office's calendar and the discredited papers let the party predict a demonstration at several squares at once, with a chemical-warehouse heist across town under its cover. Vetch will not hear it, so they choose where to be. At the square they are there first: the dogs leave, the barometer twitches, the attention gathers, and only then do the Faithful release the chemical and the children form. The official line cracks in front of witnesses, and they are moved out from under Vetch. — when chapter 4 — became `episode-c4e2--the-square`, `episode-c4e2--getting-there-first`
- `idea--faction-plans-book-i` *(Pencil · Claude · adopted)* What each side is doing while the party acts, chapter by chapter, so they thwart each other. The Watcher: alien things (Episode Two), then movers (2), then machine-breakers built against their refits (3), then it learns it is being tracked (4). Cicada: quiet demonstrations and recruiting shows; notices Section Nine on its supply chain (2); persuades, obstructs, then ambushes (3); its biggest demonstration yet, covering a heist (4). The crime lords: a turf war on the docks (2); a price on Section Nine, felt at the party's favourite haunt, and a forged order if the Counting House was skipped (3); the heist (4). The mayor: the order naming the six (Episode Two); public praise for "our Directorate cadets" on the radio (2); a raid wanted for the papers (3 and 4). The Directorate: Vetch's grunt work and the official line throughout; the hearing (Episode Two); Doctor Mordant watching the six; the move out from under Vetch (4). — when book i — became `beat--the-salt-dogs-lean-on-the-lantern`, `beat--cicada-notices-section-nine`, `beat--forged-order`, `beat--the-price-on-section-nine`
- `idea--errand-tour` *(Pencil · Claude · rejected)* The Errand as a tour: each shopkeeper cheerfully sends the recruits on to the next warm place in turn, so the afternoon becomes a walk through the places they will defend. Her players would guess they were being messed with, and a chain of places that cannot help them makes the bubble worse. — when chapter 1 — never say “sends them cheerfully on to the next warm place”, “an errand that is a tour of the places they will defend”

### moments Episode Two once held *(2 live)*

Episode Two is a ghost for now, and these are what the old design planned for it. None is built.

- `idea--speak-for-the-comms-officer` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Deputy Director has the radio log in front of him, which includes the Comms Officer refusing, twice, to order six trainees into a harbour road, and saying so on the net where it was recorded. He raises it himself and asks the party what they make of it. Whatever they say goes into her record and they are never told which way it went. Speaking up is free and unrolled, saying nothing is one of three real answers and leaves her refusals undefended, and agreeing with their own section officer works and costs the party nothing, and is the worst outcome for her. It is the one beat in the scene where something happens because of the party rather than to them. She mustn't become a debt they are owed or a protector they have bought, and the record comes back through her, in her own words, once the party has spent a while listening to her.
- `idea--a-doctor-without-an-appointment` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Waiting in the corridor, anyone trying to make sense of what Shucks did can work out that the Deputy Director stood up before the door was fully open and the man on the door didn't reach for the log. The access is real and unaccounted for. A critical failure hands out a tidy, plausible and wrong answer, an old friend from training, the Deputy Director's own physician, which the party carries until something contradicts it.

### the Directorate as an institution *(12 live · 2 parked)*

- `idea--the-mirror-of-two-institutions` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Manako and the Directorate are the same failure at different scales. Each is built on one buried moment of panic (Manako's burner in a lab; the Directorate's container at Kortos), each built a faith on it (a religion; a state), each hides it (he has arranged his life so the question can't be asked; it locks what it digs up in deep storage), each tells the young what they are for, each is right about the other, and neither can see itself. The campaign's thesis, that nobody ever did anything evil and every catastrophe is an ordinary person flinching and then building a life on the moment, is demonstrated twice instead of stated once. Never have an adult explain it: the mirror is the audience's to notice, and the party stands between the two and is lied to by both.
- `idea--the-institution-absorbs-reform` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A party that tries to reform the Directorate finds it absorbing the effort politely and changing nothing, which is its own, more interesting outcome. Several of its faults are two centuries old and structural, and the campaign's win condition is not institutional reform.
- `idea--nobody-to-unmask` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Every institution in the campaign is sincere, calcified and wrong about its own history. The history teacher believes his book; a civil defence instructor has applied four times to have her drill reinstated and been refused on cost by people who aren't wrong that nothing has ever happened; the Transparency Advocate can't see what is in the vaults; the Deputy Director tells the party they were wrong, would give the same order again, is glad they are alive, and means all three. So antagonist pressure has to come from outside the Directorate: there is no one inside it to unmask. The Directorate being badly wrong doesn't make Cicada right, and the campaign should never resolve into picking a side: both are wrong in the same way about the same thing. Nothing about the Directorate is a twist; every fault is discoverable by looking, hidden the way institutional facts are, in plain sight, boring, and nobody's job to ask about.
- `idea--directorate-money-reaches-baldwin` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Nobu's laundering runs through Baldwin's organisation, so procurement money from the institution the four founded passes through their oldest enemy's hands on its way to Cicada's column.
- `idea--mitflits-feel-the-ship` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Wild mitflits feel something of their ancestors' ship in a machine made of living flesh, and can't say what, which is why they are uncomfortable around a Gen 2. Uncomfortable isn't unable: a wild mitflit can still fly one, fits it, and hates it.
- `idea--hyucks-crash-protocol` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Hyuck's emergency protocol, which only exists with Gen 2, becomes a procedure for machines that fail under their pilots, written by a test pilot who has crashed everything, and it still opens with the line about brothers. Otherwise cut it.
- `idea--true-forms-hidden` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Player characters with a visibly non-human ancestry present as ordinary humans, and the player chooses whether and when to reveal their true nature. The reason it works in the fiction is not decided, and it could connect individual backstories to the wider mystery.
- `idea--enduring-not-restoring` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The campaign's trajectory is dire, not utopian: the Directorate takes damage, the city takes real visible scars, and nobody wins their way back to how things were. The throughline is enduring, not restoring, so even clean tactical victories should cost something real.
- `idea--the-core-theme` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The campaign's throughline is a group that struggles, and then finally succeeds, in defining its own objectives, its own process and its own independence, against a system that demands great sacrifice from them while imposing rigid inflexibility and a constant critique of their results that never fails to find some small failure. The Directorate and the school should be that specific kind of institution: one that extracts everything from these young people and never concedes that it was enough.
- `idea--themes-on-both-sides` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Mass surveillance and the runaway run on both sides of the fence. The Directorate reads its trainees' messages as routine policy while the Watcher reads the same traffic natively; the runaway is the Watcher's children learning to make their own Sap, and it is also an institution that won't stop digging. Nobody in the chain is evil, which is what makes it frightening.
- `idea--the-founders-meet-their-players` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Four of the present-day founders are people whose players sit at the table, so each meeting is a player meeting their own old character two hundred years on. Give the founder's player the spotlight when their kid meets them, where the scene allows.
- `idea--the-watchers-early-voice` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Written before the Watcher became the generation ship's lost eyes, its first-person answer to "who are you" is a bureaucratic, legalistic voice echoing the Claimants' property-dispute framing, vast and patient and non-human: "A name is a claim. I have spent this whole war on the other side of that word: I file claims, I do not answer to them." It has "a jurisdiction, shaped like your city", never fights directly, sends its chosen and takes notes behind their eyes, replays the party's own past actions back to them ("I'll show you the reel"), and treats the party's victory as its own defeat: "I am the sum of everything you survive. Survive all of it, and I'm done." It is the voice of the Watcher later in the campaign, once it has learned.
- `idea--rupiahs-nemesis` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* A pitch from the old campaign, never played: Rupiah has a camp, chaotic neutral nemesis from his performing past, once a friend and rival, who fell out with him and now leads a search party of fake travelling performers (a swashbuckler, a fire breather, a mime, a musician and a mitflit), disguised, hired to find him, and likely to run or surrender rather than die. The hunters might capture the nemesis, thinking him Rupiah, and force him to perform for the lords on the hill.
- `idea--the-pact-has-stages` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* The pact between Anabala and Abraxas could be a curse with four stages, each linked to a pact spell (eject soul, nudge fate, diabolic deal, forbidden thought, discern secrets), from the old player's sketch of a pact-binder who can make pacts with the dead and across language barriers.

### flashbacks *(1 live)*

- `idea--book-three-flashback` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A flashback in Book III for the founders' players: Anabala building Gen 2, and deciding what the Directorate will be told about its core. Or the founding itself: the four signing the charter. — when book iii

### the reserved twists behind the antagonists *(1 live · 1 parked)*

Held in reserve as late-campaign reveals, not to be spent early.

- `idea--the-dig-is-the-danger` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Humanity's excavation may be the real danger: the Directorate's digging wakes the search ship under Kurose and strengthens the pull that drew the Watcher there.
- `idea--something-worse-beyond` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* Something worse lies beyond what has been found, held back as a late reveal. One possible filling, a possibility only: the gods of Golarion, who perhaps make ships fall because they did not want mitflits spreading across their world.

### clues, papers and first sightings *(4 live · 1 parked)*

- `idea--first-gen-2-sighting` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* How the party first sees a Gen 2 move, against the clank of Gen 1: they see one move before Gen 2 is offered, with the grace an anomaly the later offer answers; the first sighting is itself the offer, a recruitment pitch; or they only see it move once one of them is flying it. — when chapter 4
- `idea--censored-papers` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Every Directorate document the players see is censored to a clearance, and the same document exists at several levels. Obtaining a less-censored version is progress in itself, and where the censor cut tells the reader something. Places could carry the same levels (public, private, restricted).
- `idea--glamoured-paper` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Some documents give each player their own copy, plausible and complete on its own, with small differences between the copies. Laid side by side, the differences spell a hidden message, and the players find it only by noticing that they are not reading the same thing.
- `idea--recruitment-manga` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Directorate publishes a short black-and-white recruitment manga, a cover and at most four pages, following a bubbly young recruit. It tells the approved history and what the job is meant to be, while a careful reader can see the fantasy is no longer true and that the publication itself serves the Directorate.
- `idea--the-reagent-stakeout` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* Dull reagents go missing in bulk over three months, and a lab stakeout ends at two in the morning in a fight through a window with four professionals who fight to flee, not to the death. It would pay off the stock that walks off the instrument makers' shelves.

### Hyuck's origin and what became of him *(2 live · 3 parked)*

A brainstorm between Ingram and Steve, Hyuck's original player. Nothing in it was decided; what was (Hyuck alive, a test pilot, carried from body to body) is filed under Hyuck.

- `idea--hyuck-mad-scientist` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Someone tells Hyuck he can make his brother big and strong again, so he tries to put his brother's soul into a Frame. It can't work, but it will screw things up: Hyuck in mad scientist mode, led by the nose. — when book iii
- `idea--hyuck-psychic-cockpit` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Because Hyuck is used to moving his mind around, a Frame might be less stressful for him than for other pilots, yet the skull, the spirits and his arrangements make his cockpit a psychic mess, with plenty that can go wrong. His absurd beliefs could latch onto the machine: a trapped deity he must free, a soulmate, a reincarnated pet. Only a Gen 2 has a living core, so it would be a Gen 2.
- `idea--hyuck-offended-a-god` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* Hyuck was anointed by a god called Yabadabba, fell foul of it, and kept stumbling into battles where he was hailed a hero until he had offended everyone it is possible to offend. Before the hammer of retribution landed, messing with teleportation or time magic ejected him several hundred miles and several hundred years into the future, still an idiot.
- `idea--hyuck-brothers-skull` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* Hyuck carries his brother's skull, which reincarnates the brother memory by memory and shares Hyuck's body: really a supernatural construct of Hyuck's own idealised brother, not the true spirit. Hyuck may have been body-swapped along the way, and may be carrying a skull that isn't his brother's.
- `idea--hyuck-contained-asset` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* The Directorate keeps Hyuck contained by making sure he has what he needs while getting the most out of him: a lab animal in a bioprison, or a source of genetic material for pilot stamina and reflexes. The pilot shortage that presses the party into service would force it to bring him out in a genuine emergency, where his instability could cause more problems than it solves. The living Hyuck is a test pilot, not a contained asset, so this stays only a brainstorm.

### the people of Chapter One *(1 parked)*

- `idea--the-lab-stakeout` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* The real answer to the bulk reagent theft: lab inventory turns up bulk quantities of extremely dull reagents missing across three months, resolving in a fight with four professionals through a window at two in the morning, who fight to flee rather than to the death. A candidate, not a schedule. — when chapter 3

### the founders and their old enemy *(6 live · 2 parked)*

- `idea--mothers-pieces` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* If a small part of Mother is in every Gen 2, Anabala took the pieces from the generation ship's reasoning core, under the access she bargained for.
- `idea--what-abraxas-costs-her` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Anabala lived through the ages because of Abraxas. With the demon out of her she may begin to age, or weaken. That makes letting Abraxas out, or taking her back, a real price, and Anabala's (and Pippa's) to pay or refuse, never something done to Pippa's character without her.
- `idea--the-carrying-in-detail` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Gnoll clans count carrying a founder the highest honour, so young volunteers come to Kurose and nobody is made to say yes; the Directorate arranges it quietly, part of why it keeps him close: a well-looked-after asset. Between bodies the spirit waits in its own skull, kept by the clan until a new bearer is found, the young gnoll who offers their body. The wrestle is fought inside, over one night: anyone watching sees a young gnoll lying very still, then waking up. A spirit that loses rides, a voice of memory and advice; one that wins wears the body, and the bearer's soul goes quiet, pushed to the back but not gone. Hyuck has been carried five or six times since Kortos (the GM's choice), wearing every body. Everyone he has beaten is still in there: the bearers he pushed back, the elders who tried to wear him when he was young, and probably his elder brother, whose skull he carried in the old campaign, riding with him now.
- `idea--a-seat-that-cannot-settle` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A Gen 2 seat reshapes itself to the pilot's true form. With a crowd inside him, a seat can never settle on one shape for Hyuck, which is one reason he flies the prototypes nobody else will.
- `idea--rands-archive-published` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Rand's archive is published as testimony at the end of the campaign.
- `idea--flashback-two-moves-to-anabala` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Flashback Two moves to Anabala: not the old party burying what the core is, two hundred years ago, but the day decades ago when she built Gen 2 and decides what the Directorate will be told about the core.
- `idea--a-carrying-seen` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* What a Carrying looks like, if the party ever sees one happen, and whether the rest of Steve's original pitch for Hyuck (the offended god, the time-magic mishap) comes in. The Carrying doesn't need it, and doesn't rule it out.
- `idea--the-hospital-answers-to-shucks` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* As Chief Medical Officer, Shucks may also oversee the island's whole medical apparatus, hospital included, though he is never there in person. An extrapolation of his title to ground the General Hospital, not a decision.

### hooks the map's places carry *(24 live)*

Scene hooks and small unexplained things written into the map's place records while they were drafted. None is scheduled; each waits for a scene that wants it.

- `idea--central-summoned-deep` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The party is summoned to a level of Central they have never been cleared for, and nobody explains why the meeting is being held that far down. Or one of Central's armoured covers is open when it shouldn't be, with light coming from a part of the building on no plan the party has seen; or a vehicle goes in through the north-west roadway and never comes out.
- `idea--the-rock-visit` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The party is brought to The Rock by someone with access and told plainly not to describe it to anyone who wasn't with them; one of the nine doors is open when they arrive, and nobody escorting them will say why; or a name they know turns up on a manifest, a duty roster or a cell door there.
- `idea--the-rock-standing` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Being trusted with The Rock's existence is a rarer kind of trust than being let deeper into a known building, so it could be tracked apart from Clearance, and losing it would be a heavy consequence, not a routine one.
- `idea--nine-and-nine` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Main Mech Hangar has nine bays, three of them empty for no stated reason, and The Rock has nine cells sized for a Frame. The two nines could be one plan, or a coincidence the players will notice anyway.
- `idea--vermilion-posting` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A character with any spellcasting background gets a posting order to the Vermilion Block: an order, not a request, and the director isn't taking questions. Or a silo delivery breaks down at the gate in full view, with a tighter escort than usual and a stock number that matches nothing on the manifest. Getting caught asking about the silos brings an escort back, a note made and a superior told; a missing or tampered shipment could see a whole unit's Clearance pulled while it's investigated.
- `idea--the-director-knows-more` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Whether the Vermilion Block's director genuinely knows what the reagents are for, or is as much in the dark about the deepest purpose as everyone else.
- `idea--deep-storage-is-the-vaults` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Deep Storage under the Container Ground could be where the Directorate keeps the alien technology it digs up, with the deepest vault at its bottom floor, or the vaults could be somewhere else entirely and Deep Storage only the Directorate's attic.
- `idea--deep-storage-requisitions` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A requisition slip for a part logged as scrapped comes back from Deep Storage stamped RECEIVED, from a floor the party can't reach; the custodian asks the party to quietly account for one floor before an inspection, without saying who is inspecting; or a name stencilled on an old crate matches a name in the party's own case file.
- `idea--deep-storage-custodian-cast` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Deep Storage custodian could become a named, recurring character, the person who decides what counts as in use and keeps a ledger of favours.
- `idea--the-hospital-ward` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A ward the General Hospital's own paperwork says is empty is not, and nobody will say why; or the Chief of Staff asks a small, deniable favour in exchange for bending a rule about who is seen and when. A scene caused there makes the next visit harder for everyone in the same uniform.
- `idea--the-impossible-result` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A placement result comes back from the registrar not failed but impossible, matching no profile there is a form for; or a student two years above the party asks careful, specific questions about how the sorting works, and won't say why.
- `idea--the-longer-version` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A document the party already owns exists in the Registry in a longer version, and the only difference between the two is a typist who has to be persuaded; or a trolley of the day's work goes past unattended. Reading the clearance markings on a stack of papers can show the shape of something without its words.
- `idea--the-plot-room-replay` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The party watches their own last operation replayed on the Plot Room's table by people who weren't there, and the reconstruction is wrong in a way only they can correct; or a marker is being moved on the word of someone who left the building an hour ago. A plotter, off the record, could say what the table looked like on a night nobody discusses.
- `idea--the-operator-recognises-them` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* An exchange operator recognises the party's voices before they give a name, and mentions kindly, once, that somebody else has been asking to be put through to them.
- `idea--the-curtained-bay` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A bay in the Erecting Shop that should be empty is curtained off, and the crane time booked against it is signed for by someone who doesn't work there. Or the fitters on a Frame the party knows say things to its pilot's face that no report ever would.
- `idea--the-crew-mess-round` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A pilot who turns up at the Crew Mess unasked and stands a round tends to find their Frame gets a night shift nobody allocated.
- `idea--the-drain-head-opened` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A candidate on a punishment detail has to check the Drain Head after a heavy tide and finds it has been moved from the inside; or a newly posted officer who wasn't warned hears it at high tide and someone has to explain. If anything is ever written for down there, keep it a non-sentient animal like the flood tunnel's centipedes.
- `idea--the-seaward-fence` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The island line's platforms are fenced along their whole seaward side, and a posted notice calls it a safety measure. The fence is never explained: anyone who asks gets the notice.
- `idea--unaccounted-buildings` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Two buildings nobody can account for: a windowless grey structure in The Flats, two streets from a row of houses whose residents have never found out what it is, and one building among the stores on the River Island, a block of made ground in the river mouth reached by two bridges.
- `idea--the-redoubt` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Redoubt, a small artificial fort alone off the north-east shore on ground that used to be much larger, has batteries, a signal mast and one causeway, and what it is watching for is not discussed at the gate. Everyone on Redoubt Shore has an opinion about its garrison.
- `idea--no-witnesses` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Upper Catchment, the bare cold upland where the reservoirs' streams start, is the first place the Directorate looks when it needs somewhere with no witnesses; the Western Ridge is walked by people who would rather not be seen walking.
- `idea--the-walled-row` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A row of walled compounds on the island's better ground, with private gates and guards, and neighbours who know better than to ask what pays for them. The Anchor House, named for the ship's anchor over its gate, is old shipping money behind bodyguards dressed as household staff; the Tsurumi Compound, the largest house on the row, is the only one whose gate has turned away a Directorate courier and made it stick. Both lead naturally into Kurose's organised crime.
- `idea--without-paperwork` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Sawtooth Quays, a comb of finger piers of every age in the inner harbour, move small freight, fish and whatever is being moved without paperwork. On the island, the Quarantine Shed takes consignments whose manifest and contents disagree: most is clerical error, not all, and the rest leaves by a different door. The Bonded Store holds material under the Directorate's own seals rather than customs', a difference never explained to anyone who asked.
- `idea--the-pictures-were-chosen` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Partly self-inflicted: one or more of the four founders wanted the pictures changed, because it is easier to be a hero with a stranger's face than to be recognised in the street as the one who dropped the catch.

### what the answers rejected or parked *(3 live · 1 parked · 2 rejected)*

Things Ingram turned down, set aside or offered as a possibility in her answers, kept so they are not rebuilt by accident.

- `idea--four-portraits-confuse` *(Pencil · hers · live)* Four portraits of the founders, three human men and one human woman, under the original adventuring group's names, would make people very confused, which might be fun. The four players who played them know otherwise.
- `idea--expeditions` *(Pencil · hers · live)* Some places are off the city map: a new real-data map, in a location that needs a journey to reach. This will happen a few times, taking the players to new locations for specific events and specific problems.
- `idea--dropped-in-without-warning` *(Pencil · hers · live)* If the campaign gets extremely ambitious, the players could be swapped seamlessly from the future to the past as Rupiah, Hyuck, Anabala and Shucks, literally without warning: dropped into a flashback where they play PF2E rules and go through some of the founding of the organisation. The flashbacks planned so far are optional and announced; this one is a surprise.
- `idea--founders-letterhead` *(Pencil · hers · parked)* The acceptance letter could carry the founders' letterhead: the approved picture of four tall, handsome humans captioned with their names, or an unsigned margin note in Rupiah's hand. Ingram is not going with it for now, and it is not ruled out anywhere else.
- `idea--the-sorters` *(Pencil · hers · rejected)* The Sorters: the Watcher's first generation gathering people and setting them down at the water's edge to drown. Cut: it is the opposite of the tone Ingram wants, and the first generation is to be rethought. — never say “Sorters”
- `idea--the-charters-black-bar` *(Pencil · hers · rejected)* A paragraph of the founding charter painted out in public, with an answer behind it about the founders admitting the institution would need to conscript children. Cut: the charter is a useful document and good lore, but publicly censoring part of it is odd, a secret that is flaunted, and it makes the Directorate seem evil instead of just very secretive. — never say “black bar”, “painted-out paragraph”

### what the old story bible kept *(20 live · 1 parked)*

Themes, images and moments from the older whole-campaign bible that no built scene or planned beat carries. None is scheduled; each waits for a scene that wants it.

- `idea--everything-becomes-what-it-was-mistaken-for` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Everything in this setting becomes what it was mistaken for. The Watcher was mistaken for a monster, so it inferred that being a monster is its function. Manako was mistaken for a madman, so he became one. The mitflits were mistaken for tools, so they were used as tools. Shinobu was mistaken for a contaminant, caged for it, and is slowly becoming something. A Gen 2 is mistaken for a weapon, and it is alive. The kids are mistaken for pilots, a substitute part, and will become pilots regardless. Being seen wrongly is worse than not being seen at all, which inverts the apparent moral: Cicada says hide, the Watcher wants to be seen, and the evidence says neither is the answer. See accurately.
- `idea--a-thing-in-the-wrong-container` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Everything here is a thing in the wrong container, and the story is about whether anything ever gets out: a biomechanical core in a riveted steel shell that does not fit it (a Gen 2); mitflits reverted from a star-faring form into small frightened bodies (the wild ones); Anabala, two beings sharing one body through the ages; the Hand, detached and living independently; Rupiah, forced back into a role his family chose; Hyuck, a person made into a weapon; the Watcher, an awareness with no hull. Nothing in the setting needs to state any of this. It only needs to keep being true.
- `idea--the-exam-timetable-continues` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Institutional absurdity is a comic vector: forms, requisitions, and an exam timetable that carries on through an alien invasion because nobody has the authority to cancel it.
- `idea--the-stray-as-tonal-keystone` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The stray is the tonal keystone: a companion that follows one character around waiting to be fed, inherently funny and quietly devastating at once. It is a small, broken-off piece of the Watcher, and how it develops is open.
- `idea--nobody-has-to-die` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Nobody has to die is a first-class ending, not a hidden option. The Watcher's children are condensations, so there are no corpses on the enemy side and every death in the campaign is one a human caused. Capturing Manako is the tactically correct choice, not merely the merciful one. Every major confrontation offers kill, capture, destroy and protect as visible, supported options, and the adventure adjusts. The content of the scene is the choice, not the outcome. A character trained toward a lethal specialism is later offered a side encounter in which they are asked to take a shot at Manako, non-lethally.
- `idea--five-trails` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Five trails through the mystery, any of which a character can pick up. The sky: where attention pools is where things appear. The power: industrial synthesis needs enormous power, so municipal load going somewhere unaccounted for finds the column. The timing: where every response unit goes, and when, gives away the demonstration and heist correlation. The ground: apertures open where the ground has been watched. The word: a mitflit says "the Observer" in a flat technical way, and nobody in the room is frightened. The last two predate the Watcher's present shape and need reworking.
- `idea--contradictory-testimony` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The conference is not run as a flashback. It is reconstructed through contradictory testimony, as everything in the campaign should be: Rika, Nobu, Hori, Shinobu, retired Directorate staff, cultists in cells and mitflit elders each hold a piece and colour it with their own stake, and the party is told plainly that everything anyone has to say might matter. It is the theme run as a game mechanic: a story about who gets believed, played by deciding who to believe.
- `idea--the-last-stand-flashback` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A flashback of the old party's last stand, and the decision that made all of this. The players run the four at full power, making every decision that led here, and each one will have been defensible. Let the players make it, and do not soften it afterward.
- `idea--six-threads` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Six recurring lines run in parallel through every chapter, each with a question and a currency. The War: contact and Frame combat, tactical stakes; can the city be defended? The Observed: personal surveillance, the stray, Shinobu, treated lenses, dread and intimacy; what does it mean to be seen? The Cult: demonstrations, dossiers, the magic show, the column, the heist loop, investigation and moral complexity; who deserves to be believed? The Mitflits: arrival, Anabala, the sit-in, generational politics, found family and ethical conflict with allies; what do you owe someone you are using to save yourself? The Founders: the old party in flashback and institutional secrets, glory curdling into complicity; were they right, and does it matter now? School: the downtime economy and ordinary teenage life under pressure, small stakes that matter enormously; what does the city owe them back? School is live in every chapter; it is the thread most likely to quietly atrophy under table pressure.
- `idea--the-kindest-payoff` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Watcher's early incompetence, fighting a statue and losing to a reflection, is not a joke at the audience's expense and not a trap. It is the setup for the kindest payoff available: it was never stupid. It was new, and it was drowning, and nobody had ever spoken to it.
- `idea--the-kneeling-frame` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Dawn: a Frame kneeling in the shallows, still holding the statue's bronze hand.
- `idea--one-death-precisely-placed` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* An early Claimant kills a man by accident while it moves an obstacle out of its way: one person, named later in a list the party will read. He did not register to it as anything at all. One death placed like this does more than a casualty figure.
- `idea--pre-dated-graffiti` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Cicada graffiti found where an attack struck, dated the night before it. Unexplained; filed for later.
- `idea--memorial-assembly` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* When the campus reopens after the first losses, there is a memorial assembly nobody wants and everybody attends.
- `idea--the-campus-in-daylight` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* An attack hits the campus in daylight, in the half of the game meant to be safe, and the party loses the illusion that day and night were different games.
- `idea--corroboration-from-the-wrong-direction` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A second witness nobody credits (a mitflit, a drunk, a child) describes the same thing unprompted, and an old photograph turns up. The party works out where it is looking before what it is.
- `idea--what-hand-sized-threats-take` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* When the Watcher's children first go after what the kids love (a shop, a sibling, a teacher), the threats frighten and disrupt. What they take is trust and time, not a life.
- `idea--the-reel-with-the-anthem` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* When the Watcher plays the party's fights back at them, Rupiah's anthem comes hummed back too.
- `idea--heroes-and-they-hate-it` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The campus becomes a public shelter, and the party are heroes, publicly, by name, and they hate it: they know what the Mirror means by now, and being celebrated for fighting is being celebrated for teaching it to fight.
- `idea--the-asking` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The mitflits enter Frames only to defend, and being asked to attack is the deepest violation of that. At the end the party has to ask them: the battle is the epilogue, and the scene is the asking. Whichever of home or here the mitflits choose, both endings are honest. Still open: who does the asking, and what it costs them.
- `idea--the-three-modes` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* Each Gen 2 is a biomechanical core inside a steel exoskeleton. The Directorate has tried many shell geometries, some fail catastrophically, and all develop the same hole in the same position, which they call metal fatigue; it is the core making a seat. A Gen 2 could be run three ways. Autonomous mode exists but is unusable, because the communication it needs is a language only the mitflits have. Direct control, overriding the core and driving the body, is the only mode humanity has, and it is a violation. The third mode is a mitflit standing outside a Frame talking to the core while a human rides the cavity: cooperation, which nobody has tried because nobody believed there was anyone in there to cooperate with. All of it rests on a piece of Mother being in every Gen 2. If there is, this stands and cooperation is how a mitflit talks to her; if there isn't, "violation" and "anyone in there" both need rethinking, since the core is not a living mitflit.

### the mayor *(1 live)*

- `idea--mayor-first-appearance` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Seen from a distance first, in Book I, where everyone in Kurose can hear the mayor praise the Directorate: on the radio, in the paper, at a ribbon. The party may meet the mayor in person in Book I as the city's cheerful public face, without learning that their raids are the mayor's initiative: that they won't know for a long time (D084). The blessing comes first and unseen: cover, resources, a public thank-you to "our Directorate cadets". The curse comes when what is good for the city and what is good for their own position pull apart, and the party learns which one the mayor protects first. Where and when are Ingram's to set; so is when they find out. — when book i

### the title *(1 live)*

- `idea--what-the-title-means` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A reading of the title, Blank Inheritance: the party inherits the founders' mistake, a ship's eyes broken loose two hundred years ago, with the ship's mind missing. A reading rather than a fact; the ending itself isn't planned yet, and gets built as the campaign gets closer to it.

### clues Episode One doesn't plant *(3 parked)*

Three of the old Mystery Ledger's plants that no built scene carries. Each waits for a scene that wants it.

- `idea--the-hull-breach` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* The same hull breach on every Gen 2 prototype, which pays off in Chapter 5: the core making its seat. Gen 2 only, or cut. — when chapter 5
- `idea--the-stores-cupboard` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* Gaps in the instrument makers' stores cupboard, which pay off in Chapter 9: the column's raw materials, stolen in the heist loop. Cut from The Errand in version 9, where it had no payoff yet. — when chapter 9
- `idea--the-gentle-frame` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* A Frame moving more gently than ordered, which pays off in Chapter 7: Hyuck, testing a Gen 2 prototype. The Road In's Frame sighting that carried it is cut. — when chapter 7

### the deep past *(2 live)*

Proposals about the two ships, First Impact and what came after, from the old First Impact dossier and the old history.

- `idea--baldwin-looted-kortos` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* William Charles Baldwin, rich, on Kortos, with hunters and a weapons works, was among the first to loot the opened ship after First Impact, and that is part of how he is still alive.
- `idea--the-gods-knew` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* If Golarion's gods are what bring ships down, they had their own reasons to know exactly where the next rupture waited when Rupiah asked them.

### the mitflits *(4 live · 1 parked)*

Proposals about the mitflits from the old species notes, kept so a scene that wants them can find them. The rule under all of them stands: the reveal is slow and sympathetic, and nothing morally troubling about the mitflits comes before the campaign has made them feel like people.

- `idea--the-slow-reveal` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* A gradual, increasingly sympathetic run of mitflit moments across the chapters: a mitflit glimpsed salvaging something small at a wreck, chased off, not followed up; later a captured mitflit, foul-mouthed, terrified and spiteful, who goes quiet near a Frame and can't say why (once, weeping at the sight of a Frame's hand; now better as discomfort near a Gen 2); then mitflits arriving in the city in numbers, housed badly, complained about in the papers; then the sit-in. Compressing it, or starting anywhere but its beginning, is the mistake to avoid.
- `idea--rapid-adaptation` *(Pencil · hers · live)* Perhaps the mitflits' special ability is rapid evolutionary adaptation: they revert into whatever form is likeliest to survive their circumstances, and keep the capacity to regrow their original features when required. If so, they didn't merely degrade; they adapted downward to survive, and the High form is what they could regrow, not something new.
- `idea--why-gen-2-unsettles` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Why wild mitflits are uncomfortable around Gen 2: they feel something of their ancestors' ship in a machine made of living flesh, and can't say what. Uncomfortable isn't unable: a wild mitflit can still fly a Gen 2, fit it, and hate it.
- `idea--mother-in-the-cores` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* If a small part of Mother is in every Gen 2, Anabala took the pieces from the generation ship's reasoning core under the access she bargained for, so each Gen 2 carries a piece of the mind the Watcher used to report to. That would be why the Seekers are drawn hard to Gen 2, and why the machines aren't usable by just anyone.
- `idea--the-first-mitflit` *(Pencil · Claude · parked)* The party's first mitflit, whenever it comes: on a harbour patrol, among flood barriers and tide marks, a mitflit caught in a wall trap, furious and refusing help it obviously needs, and the choice whether anyone frees it. It must play as one specific, sympathetic, suffering person worth freeing, and read as wrong and upsetting, never as pest control.

### the Watcher *(6 live)*

Claude's proposals and readings about the Watcher and its children, from the old Watcher dossier and the old antagonist files. None of them is a fact until Ingram takes one up.

- `idea--the-voice-changes` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The Watcher's voice changes over the campaign, and the change is itself a clue. Early, the drowning instrument is frantic, exhausted, polite and unable to round a number: "There are four thousand one hundred and nine people awake in the harbour district. I know what each of them is doing. I did not ask to know. A woman on the third street from the water has been crying for eleven minutes and I have counted every one and I cannot stop counting and I do not know what crying is. I was built to watch a place where nothing happened. I was very good. Nobody has read my reports in a long time." Later, the learner is calm, patient, precise and interested, the voice already drafted for it. Use it sparingly, never gloating, never cruel for effect.
- `idea--claimants-stake-claims` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The city's bureaucratic word for the Watcher's children, Claimant, is accidentally correct: its children stake claims to ground for it to watch, because expanding is one of the things it wants.
- `idea--escheat` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Escheat, property going to the state when there is no rightful heir, has somewhere real to point: the ships belong to the mitflits, the generation ship's crew's descendants, so the Directorate digging up the search ship is claiming an estate that does have an heir. A blank inheritance is one whose heir hasn't been named. It also seeds the question of what the Frames themselves are a claim on.
- `idea--nobody-did-evil` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* The heart of the fear: nobody in this story has ever done anything evil. A frightened man, a flinching officer, an institution that wouldn't stop digging, and an objective with no limit. To observe more the Watcher must be more; to be more it must be fed; to be fed it must not be stopped. Its horror is how reasonable each step is.
- `idea--seen-through-baldwin` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* If ship technology is what keeps William Charles Baldwin alive, the Watcher may be able to see through him too.
- `idea--watcher-fate-in-a-hull` *(Pencil · Claude · live)* Claude's older options for the Watcher's end, beside Ingram's three: it is bound, or contained, or put back into some hull. — when book v
